items.title: Add the Grafana connector
items.body:
<!-- replay source=https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/issues/826 -->
> Replayed from sandbox-quantum/switch issue 826 for the Maintainer Room demo.

## What
A Grafana connector, so that someone who connects their Grafana account in Switch Console can let their agents query Grafana Cloud dashboards, metrics and logs, as them.

## Why
Grafana is the default dashboard for many teams' metrics and logs.

## How
Grafana Cloud has an official remote MCP server at `https://mcp.grafana.com/mcp`, OAuth only; most clients register automatically ([docs](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/ai-tools/mcp-servers/cloud-mcp/)). It needs Grafana Assistant on the stack, and MCP users count as Assistant users for billing (say so in the description). Self-hosted Grafana is out of scope.

Add a new entry, `core/switch_core/connections/catalog/grafana/`.

Follow **[Adding a connector](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/blob/main/docs/design/service-connections-v2.md#adding-a-connector)** in the service connections v2 design doc. A connector is usually a catalog entry plus a skill, with no code, in one of three shapes:
1. a remote MCP server with OAuth (example: `catalog/atlassian/`)
2. a command-line tool with OAuth (example: `catalog/google-workspace/`)
3. a key the person pastes in (`adapter: api_key`, with `mcp` or `cli`; example: `catalog/datadog/`)

Prefer OAuth with dynamic registration where the vendor offers it, then a static OAuth app, then a key, and say in the PR why you chose that shape. If the vendor fits none of them, comment on this issue before writing broker code.

Locally, turn connections on with `FEATURE_FLAGS_ENABLED=service_connections`.

**Rules every connector follows:**
- The token or key never reaches the coding tool (env, args or files); the session host makes the calls
- Ask for the least access that works: no admin, org-wide or delete scopes without a written reason. Offer a read-only level if the vendor supports one
- OAuth stays strict: HTTPS, PKCE S256, no new redirect hosts; don't loosen the loader's checks
- CLIs run without a shell, from the vendor's official release pinned by SHA-256, with auth/config/admin commands denied
- No real data in the repo: no tokens, tenant URLs or account ids in fixtures or screenshots
- The logo is the official mark (viewBox and paths only), credited in `NOTICE.md`

## Done when
- [ ] `connections/catalog/grafana/connection.yaml` is complete and `enabled: true`, with comments on anything the vendor needs turned on and anything measured rather than documented (e.g. token lifetime)
- [ ] `skill/SKILL.md` describes the tasks, tools and limits, with safe defaults (read before writing, confirm before deleting or closing), and never mentions credentials
- [ ] It shows up in Switch Console's Connections with its name and logo, and connecting works (read-only and read-write, if both are offered)
- [ ] Granted to an agent, its tools work in a session from a room; turning the grant off stops the session's access within a minute
- [ ] An expiring token is renewed without the user doing anything (OAuth)
- [ ] Disconnecting removes access (and revokes at the vendor where possible; for keys, the UI says Switch can't revoke them)
- [ ] The token or key appears nowhere in the transcript, the room or the logs
- [ ] Loader tests for the entry (`core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_loader.py`)
- [ ] A short video of connect → grant → agent uses it in a room → grant off

## Out of scope
Webhooks from the vendor into rooms; tool classification by level; connecting from the web dashboard.

items.body:
Tracked by #42. Milestone: v0.2.0. Status: planned; implementation begins after prerequisite gates.

## Outcome and scope

Ship Python connector SDK and local conformance runner.

Specification trace: EXT-01 completion. Local planning source: docs/phases/phase-2-graph-ownership-entitlements.md. Public tickets summarize the design; private plans/specification are not to be copied into PRs.

## Dependencies and ownership

Depends on: Previous phase exit gate and stable shared contracts.

Primary ownership: sdk/python; connector language-neutral tests; scaffolder. One ticket per agent and feature branch. Coordinate shared contracts with sibling PRs before edits; rebase and validate against merged prerequisites before readiness.

## Step-by-step execution

1. Read AGENTS.md, openwiki/index.md and relevant linked pages; verify current source/tests and accepted ADRs. Read the owning phase, specification sections above, CONTRIBUTING.md, LICENSING.md and PR template. Existing proposals are working choices, not proof of validation.
2. Write or update OpenAPI/protobuf/JSON Schema and migration/interface contracts before changing public behavior. Specify failure states and tenant/evidence ownership.
3. Implement Python worker binding to the stable Phase 1 HTTP/gRPC contract and shared schemas. Add Python connector scaffolder and run same fixture-based conformance suite as Go. Document version compatibility and secure diagnostics.
4. Add deterministic positive/negative/partial/unknown tests and targeted cross-tenant/secret-canary checks. Use sanitized recorded fixtures as primary CI input; live provider checks require consented test estates and explicit edition/permission coverage.
5. Run affected package tests and compatibility/codegen checks, then make test, make build and git diff --check. Record exact commands, versions, failures and unavailable tools. Extend docs and requirement status with evidence; refresh OpenWiki through its integration.
6. Open a draft PR to main, signed-off commits, using the PR template and a body file. Reference this issue; use Closes only when every acceptance item passes. Include source decisions, migration/rollback implications, test evidence and any remaining gaps. Never merge automatically.

## Architecture and security requirements

Go backend; static Next.js export embedded in Go; PostgreSQL authoritative ledger/governance state; rebuildable projections. Preserve separate collection, governance, execution and runtime-access identities. The friendly CLI must not link custody/actions. One server authorization path plus RLS; scope caches/jobs/exports and graph results. SecretRef outside custody; no secret values/customer data in logs, traces or fixtures. Preserve evidence/provenance and time bounds, unknown is not safe, failed collection is not deletion, provider acknowledgment is not verification. Pin dependency versions and CI action SHAs; use least-privilege tokens and no untrusted code with write credentials. Preserve configured telemetry behavior while isolating test configuration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Go/Python produce equivalent sanitized envelopes and failure states; compatibility mismatch fails explicitly; packages build locally and signed/trusted publication is gated through release process.
- [ ] Contracts, generated outputs, schema/migration compatibility, documentation and requirement evidence agree.
- [ ] Focused failure and authorization tests pass; partial/unavailable results are explicit.
- [ ] Required checks have linked evidence; no fabricated test success or later-phase feature claims.
- [ ] PR has an ownership boundary, prerequisite links, test results and rollout/recovery notes.

items.title: feat(mcp): implement secure outbound MCP connector router
items.body:
## Objective
Implement the central outbound MCP connector plane defined in PR #31. UGAI must reach upstream MCP services only through IM19.

## Scope
- Typed operator-managed connector registry with immutable revisions.
- Outbound MCP Streamable HTTP client using fixed registered endpoints only.
- Namespaced tool discovery and collision rejection.
- Per-connector/per-tool default-deny policy, verified subject and tenant enforcement.
- Secret-manager references, bounded requests/results, timeouts and concurrency limits.
- SSRF defenses plus network egress policy requirements.
- Redacted durable audit before/after execution; fail closed on audit failure.
- Approval workflow for mutating tools; read-only-only initial release.
- Tests for DNS rebinding, private/link-local/metadata IPs, redirects, tenant isolation, spoofed tools, schema abuse, replay, audit outage, oversized responses and timeouts.

## Explicitly out of scope for initial router release
- Direct public access to local DaVinci Resolve MCP.
- Unrestricted shell/filesystem tools.
- Enabling mutating provider tools by default.

## Acceptance
- Staging IM19 HTTPS endpoint with real OAuth.
- At least one non-production upstream MCP connected end-to-end through IM19.
- UGAI calls only IM19; no direct upstream MCP endpoint configuration in UGAI.
- Security and regression suites pass; monitoring and rollback documented.
- Keep feature disabled until all gates pass.

items.title: [Spec] P5 — Evidence, outcomes and business validation
items.body:
# P5 — Evidence, outcomes and business validation

Parent specification and coordination: https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/5

Status: ready for manager decomposition after assignment. No implementation, paid experiments or rollout dispatched by this issue.

## Problem Statement

Artists need useful recommendations but available metrics differ in definition, age and completeness. Without explicit evidence and workflow measurement, Relay could optimize vanity metrics or mistake feature activity for recurring value.

## Solution

Provide deterministic, provenance-bearing facts and outcomes to the manager, and measure whether the complete service saves artist effort and supports a viable recurring business.

## User Stories

1. As an artist, I want to see unavailable metrics distinguished from zero, so that missing data does not look like failure.
2. As an artist, I want to know whether a number is a captured total or period change, so that I can interpret it correctly.
3. As an artist, I want to see evidence tied to the right work and platform publication, so that unrelated performance does not influence my plan.
4. As an artist, I want to have commissions or memberships assessed separately from likes, so that my actual goal remains visible.
5. As an artist, I want to label outcomes I report myself, so that Relay does not imply independent verification.
6. As an artist, I want to see attribution uncertainty, so that estimates are not presented as proven conversions.
7. As an artist, I want to understand why a next-cycle change is suggested, so that I can accept or reject it intelligently.
8. As an operator, I want to measure completed releases and artist effort, so that we can distinguish useful management from queue activity.
9. As an operator, I want to measure repeat catalogue use and recurring sessions, so that we can test the archive's ongoing value.
10. As an operator, I want to measure model, storage, support and connector costs, so that subscription viability is assessed honestly.

## Implementation Decisions

- Own metric definitions, deterministic fact assembly, coverage/freshness, outcome semantics and workflow-value instrumentation. Reuse PiecePerformanceFacts, Goal Cycle fact packs, attribution/outcome snapshots and learning proposals.
- Preserve Work/Bundle, Relay Post and Platform Instance distinctions. Do not equate incompatible network metrics or relabel captured totals as period changes.
- Evidence records carry source, window/baseline, freshness, availability reason and attribution class. Latest unavailable observations must not silently resurrect older values as current evidence.
- Bind outcomes to plan/action/publication references; replayed receipts and observations cannot double-count success. Preparation completion is not publication completion.
- Supply facts for business goals where evidence exists; distinguish creator-reported, deterministic, estimated and unknown outcomes. Do not invent attribution when linkage is unavailable.
- Separate facts, generated interpretation and proposed experiments. P2/P3 own explanation behavior and grounding evaluation; P5 does not change measurements to fit a narrative.
- Design privacy-conscious telemetry for time/effort, corrections, repeat cycles, archive reuse, delivery failures and operating cost. Avoid raw private captions, patron identities or credentials in analytics metadata.
- Prepare a comparison/pilot protocol with baseline workflow and predeclared decision criteria. Running outreach, charging participants, changing prices or claiming validated demand is outside this specification.

## Testing Decisions

- Primary seam: authenticated evidence/outcome reads over real saved publication and plan records. Add focused deterministic metric tests where arithmetic and missingness require exact assertions.
- Cover stale/null data, unknown versus zero, baseline gaps, duplicate receipts, ambiguous links, changed source references and tenant isolation.
- Estimated conversions cannot satisfy a deterministic conversion target; likes do not substitute for sales.
- Prior art: PiecePerformanceFacts, Goal Cycle outcome/learning tests and attribution isolation integration. Feed the same evidence fixtures to P3 rather than parallel invented metric logic.

## Out of Scope

Exhaustive historical metrics, new scraping/trend providers, guaranteed growth, new attribution infrastructure without source evidence, billing changes, paid-pilot execution or external contact.

## Further Notes

Can inventory facts, publish definitions and build synthetic fixtures immediately. Integration needs P1 provenance, P2 plan/goal identity, P4 receipts and P6 correction/effort events. Exit: the manager can explain a completed or partial cycle from truthful facts, and the proposed pilot can distinguish usefulness, publication success and commercial outcomes.

The parent issue defines shared contract ownership, parallel waves, integration acceptance and shared-file serialization. Test boundaries were confirmed by the user: shared authenticated application operations, with focused connector and AI-quality evaluation seams. Preserve existing safety, approval and release requirements; reconcile older conflicting priorities with the current artist-manager direction.

Related pipelines: [P1](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/6) · [P2](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/7) · [P3](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/8) · [P4](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/9) · [P6](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/11). Integration dependencies are described above; these links do not make all work wait for other pipelines to finish.

items.title: [MOD-002 P8a READINESS] Reversible catalog master lifecycle and archived roster contract (no build)
items.body:
## Scope — MOD-002 P8a readiness, NOT a BUILD dispatch

**Purpose:** Source-audit and specify **reversible Active/Inactive lifecycle and complete archived roster** for Unit, Brand, Category masters so the existing HisabIQ Product Settings screen can eventually connect without losing behavior. **Planning/contract review only**: no code, migration, data changes, branch, deployment, UI cutover, or automatic merges are authorized by this issue.

### Paired verified source pins (2026-11-14; recheck at dispatch)
- Backend: `shuvodelux-commits/nestshererp` branch `chore/hisabiq-adoption-runtime-a01@9395cf57110649a6bd845572c79c6f101750849c`.
- Frontend: `shuvodelux-commits/hisabiq_ui/main@e30aa0a47e2f68142c5a01a7bba39fef5d7b6bf9`.
- Existing relevant sources: `packages/core-application/src/catalog/manage-catalog-service.ts`, `catalog-repository.ts`, PostgreSQL `schema.ts`, Nest `catalog.controller.ts`, and `src/components/products/ProductSettings.tsx`.
- Dependency: P7e [frontend draft PR #565](https://github.com/shuvodelux-commits/hisabiq_ui/pull/565) has exact-head QA/CI evidence but is **unmerged and awaiting independent review/owner gate**. P5c [draft #519](https://github.com/shuvodelux-commits/hisabiq_ui/pull/519) is **not live**.

### Confirmed source facts / architectural hazards
1. Current legacy `removeUnit/Brand/Category` uses `countReferences` to **hard-delete if not referenced**, or **archive (deleted_at)** if referenced; this is **not** a reversible Active/Inactive toggle. Category children can block removal.
2. Metadata-v1 GET currently omits archived masters; usage-v1 includes archive references and inactive-product references. Two independent GETs have no shared revision and cannot authorize destructive mutation.
3. The frontend Product Settings has reversible Activate/Deactivate actions plus Active/Inactive badges. It also displays counts, Bangla/English name edits, unit kind, categories and Defaults. A narrower API must not replace or silently disable those existing UI behaviors.
4. Legacy product reference counters require independent source review for `product_unit_conversions` and non-stock documents: a partial count is not sufficient to prove a unit/brand/category is never used. No destructive change should rely on the non-atomic frontend usage count.

### Required READINESS deliverable (issue comments are sufficient; backend AGENTS.md forbids ad hoc new Markdown)
- Create a **REUSE / ADAPT / EXTEND / BLOCKED** action-to-contract matrix for all three master kinds, distinguishing reversible `inactive` from `archived` and genuinely hard-deleted states, including uniqueness and name reuse.
- Define an explicit lifecycle state machine and historical visibility/read contract without assuming `deleted_at` equals inactive; preserve old posted/stock/product references and tenant isolation. Distinguish archival due to historical use from deliberate user deactivation.
- Propose strict versioned `GET roster`, `PATCH status` and restore/safe-remove command semantics with required current session/permissions, 404 cross-tenant and 409 stale-version handling. The final endpoint shapes and any schema amendment require owner signoff.
- Specify **atomic server-side** referential preflight for any delete/archive/restore, referencing all relevant product, conversion, category child and historical links; include row-level locks or equivalent concurrency control. Do not accept an advisory frontend count as authorization.
- Explicit migration/RLS/backfill/rollback/dual-read plan for any proposed state column or archived roster, including legacy archived rows without fabricating activation history; do not reserve/execute migration without approval.
- Produce a future implementation test matrix: both tenants and permissions, active/inactive/archived visibility; rename/status and category-parent conflicts, simultaneous references, stale version, duplicate name/reuse, in-use remove refusal, orphaned conversion links, interrupted/duplicate requests, 0 stock/journal/cash side effects, audit/outbox atomicity, restored reference integrity and signed React keyboard/touch acceptance.
- Separate dependencies **not in P8a**: Base/Compound-ready unit classification, nested category parent editing, Product Defaults mapping, advanced product multi-unit pricing/snapshots, all deferred UI activation.

### Release and ownership rules
- Read both repositories' `AGENTS.md` first and current source before recommending a contract. Do not refactor unrelated modules or touch shared schema while concurrent module workers own it.
- Return a concise proposed contract and source-evidence matrix for owner review. Mark **BLOCKED / OWNER DECISION REQUIRED** for unresolved status semantics or destructive data paths.
- After owner explicitly approves a bounded implementation slice, dispatch **one isolated task** with allowed files, owner/runner, current baseline SHAs and disposable PostgreSQL16; use mandatory approved `/super-build` and exhaustive scenario-backed tests, GitHub CI, independent QA and draft PR. No merge/deploy/production operations without explicit owner authorization.

**Status: READINESS ONLY — NOT APPROVED FOR BUILD.**

items.body:
## Parent / Authority

Scoped Kubernetes Tenant Overview UI refinement under #730 (approved Tenant Overview hierarchy), integrated UAT authority #125, and Design System #572. Use `docs/design/components/OPERATIONAL_SECTION_CARD.md`, `app/templates/components/operational_section_card.html`, `section_link_button.html`, and `table_label.html` as the canonical component owners.

## Human UAT Finding (2026-10-25)

On **Kubernetes → Tenant → Overview**, two separate `Needs Attention` and `Recent Tenant Activity` cards fragment a single operational narrative and consume unnecessary header/surface space. The operator reviewed and approved a visual concept with **one unified attention/activity surface**, preserving differentiated severity and event status.

## Bounded Implementation

- Replace the two outer cards with **one** KAORI Operational Section Card titled `Operational Attention & Activity`, with two accessible internal sections (priority findings and latest committed activity).
- Reuse the canonical shared card geometry, semantic status labels, and section action links; **one** action in the outer header per the approved component standard, with the other action in the associated internal section header.
- Show compact, clearly *preview-scoped* counts for critical/warning and recent events derived only from already bounded committed rows. Do not present limited rows as fleet-wide totals.
- Responsive desktop dual-column / narrow-device stacked presentation with independent empty states; preserve full source-backed titles, types, status, details, event timestamps, and links to Intelligence and Tenant Operations Activity.
- Preserve existing source context (`tenant_attention_rows`, `tenant_recent_activity_rows`), RBAC, provider authority, sync, persistence, and routes. No external provider calls, schema changes, mutations, new shared component, or CSS library.
- Update the owning Tenant Overview contract tests and architecture/readme guidance for single-card composition, accessible actions, count semantics, and no-data states.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One outer shared card; both logical areas remain visible, with intact evidence and actions.
- Counts are preview-scoped, never fabricated full finding totals; status remains semantic and source-backed.
- Light/dark, 1280/1024 desktop, 390/360 mobile, keyboard navigation/focus, no unintended page-level overflow.
- Jinja render, djlint, focused pytest, visual QA and human DevContainer UAT before acceptance; record actual tests/evidence on exact SHA.
- Deliver through scoped branch and temporary `kaori/review/staging-uat` holding branch only. **Official Developer Check, Full Admission, staging/main promotion, deploy, tag and release HOLD until explicit operator authorization.**

## Exclusions

Do not redesign Tenant Estate, Multi-Cluster Posture, background sync, Intelligence/Activity routes, or unrelated historical QA failures in this UI workstream.

items.title: Expose brand campaigns and publishing readiness through MCP

labels.name: human-review
labels.description: Needs manual QA by a human before it counts as done

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Problem
The bounded default MCP catalog exposes scheduling but omits brand publishing readiness. Discovery describes the readiness operation, yet clients that only load tools/list cannot invoke it without reconnecting. Publish Campaigns already exist (#4120), but MCP discovery currently exposes only provider Ads campaign reporting, leaving native content campaigns inaccessible.

## Authorized outcome
Extend the existing brand-scoped Campaign model with reusable creative context and asset membership, expose campaign operations through MCP, preserve campaign identity through generation and scheduled releases, and prove the complete workflow. Reuse existing publishing approvals and tenant-scoped services.

## Implementation claim
Codex owns this follow-up. Open PR and issue searches found no overlapping active implementation. Existing genfeedai/growth#5 owns private launch execution; this issue owns product capability. Preserve unrelated in-flight MCP metadata work (#7418) and the canonical MCP migration (#7845).

## Acceptance criteria

Source implementation and verification are complete. PR genfeedai/genfeed.ai#7853 merged at c422ba5821741a6f7b350ef1737e999401baec1d with required source CI green and the matching master rule evaluation PASS. Deployment and authenticated live acceptance remain pending; this issue stays open until that final criterion passes.
- [x] A default-profile MCP caller can read an explicitly selected brand's publishing readiness before scheduling, retaining role and connector permission checks.
- [x] Native Campaign CRUD is available through MCP using the existing Campaign service and serializer contracts.
- [x] Campaigns retain goal/brief, audience, voice/direction and selected Library assets within the owning organization and brand.
- [x] Campaign context participates in campaign content generation; inherited brand context remains available.
- [x] Campaign identity survives creation of draft/scheduled releases and their targets.
- [x] Cross-tenant, cross-brand, deleted and invalid asset/release references are rejected.
- [x] Retries do not duplicate campaign records or scheduled releases.
- [x] Scheduling preserves existing validation and server-enforced approval.
- [x] Existing Publish UI can inspect/edit campaign context and assets using established components.
- [x] Regression-first focused tests, affected typechecks/build checks and current-head required CI pass.
- [ ] After deployment, authenticated MCP reads and the authorized content-campaign workflow are verified.

## Approach
Compare expanding the existing Campaign domain against tags-only grouping and a separate campaign/publisher implementation. Extend the existing Campaign domain: durable identity and context with asset/release links, no duplicate publishing engine. Implement and verify the MCP readiness repair before continuing campaign implementation. Stop the affected workflow and fix each encountered bug.

## Verification
Exercise actual MCP schemas/transport, campaign persistence/ownership and serializer behavior, generation context, campaign-to-release lineage, and Publish UI behavior. Implementation verification is performed by Codex; separate model review not requested. Private campaign copy, operational strategy and publishing receipts remain outside this public issue.

items.title: [CONN-CRM-003] Add a qualified HubSpot inbound adapter for the SMB relationship import
items.body:
Todo-ID: CONN-CRM-003
State: OPEN

## Outcome
Add a HubSpot-specific inbound adapter that feeds the proposed SMB-CRM-007 mapped and provenanced relationship import/export workflow. A company admin connects one HubSpot account, confirms the provider portal identity, binds it to one HCM company, chooses the supported company/contact projection, maps fields, previews the exact import outcomes, and activates a recoverable inbound sync. HubSpot remains the source for its CRM objects and pipeline activity. This ticket adds no second generic import engine and does not claim a production HubSpot connector or business-party registry already exists.

## Workflow, field authority, and shared owners
From Admin → Integrations (proposed provider detail extension), the admin enters the proposed HubSpot connection flow, reviews requested scopes and distribution status, confirms the returned portal/account identifier, and binds it to one HCM company. The exact current-platform authorization flow must be established in the test portal before production activation. The supported object/field matrix is explicit and versioned. HubSpot owns external record IDs, its pipeline/activity state, and fields the tenant marks HubSpot-authoritative. HCM owns business-party roles/sites, contact affiliations, local access and review decisions. The initial direction is inbound observation or staging into the SMB-CRM-007 target. No automatic email/name matching, merge, contact deletion, or outbound field write is allowed. A later outbound action must be separately authorized against field ownership and current revision.

Reuse `internal/connectivity/application/installation.go` for connection lifecycle, `internal/connectivity/mapping` and `mappingprofile` for field maps, `syncjob` for checkpoints, `providerreceipt`/`observe` for source evidence, and `operation`, reconciliation, capacity, and health owners for transport outcomes. The relationship import target is SMB-CRM-007 (#3527); it owns generic mapping, provenance, preview, row recovery, and import/export semantics. This ticket owns HubSpot portal binding, provider descriptors and object/field fixtures, supported pagination or event-to-observation translation, and account-specific authorization diagnostics. Existing `internal/domains/crm` is recruiting/talent CRM and must not be repurposed as the customer registry. Shared connector authentication, schema, mapping, webhook, cursor, replay, and health engines remain shared prerequisites.

## Qualification and interaction
Use the current HubSpot Developer Platform app path and minimum required scopes only after verifying them in a test portal. The linked official page documents the legacy public-app path and is historical context, not instructions for new app setup. Verify current OAuth installation, scope classification, allowlisted or Marketplace distribution, and review/unverified-install behavior directly before enabling a tenant. Before activation, qualify current platform registration, OAuth and refresh behavior, exact company/contact endpoints and scopes, API quota/retry semantics, app review/distribution, target account eligibility, and schema/version change behavior using a test portal. If the installed app is unverified or the account lacks a required feature, show a qualification hold and do not imply production support.

The proposed flow shows Connect, verified portal identity, Bind company, Select objects, Map, Preview, Activate, Health, Reconnect, and Disconnect. Preview identifies creates, updates, unchanged rows, ambiguous records, forbidden fields, and source revisions. Loading, empty schema, denied scope, wrong portal/company, revoked auth, stale schema, rate limiting, conflicting revision, duplicate event, and expired cursor each have an explicit state and recovery action. Cursor expiry requires snapshot reconciliation before resume. Disconnect fences new sync and keeps pending operations inspectable. Reuse existing Admin integration/operations pages and shared forms, tables, alerts, and dialogs; add a provider detail extension only where needed. Keep keyboard order and focus visible, associate errors with inputs, announce async state, support en-US/de-DE/RTL, and fit narrow responsive layouts.

## Acceptance and rollout
Tests prove a wrong portal cannot bind to another company; repeated provider record/event identity and revision does not create duplicate parties; ambiguous email/name matches require review; API permission failure does not advance the cursor; revoked access pauses before external calls; and stale schema/cursor requires repair or reconciliation instead of silently skipping data. Cross-company external IDs cannot be resolved by guessing a tenant. Require SMB-CORE-002 and SMB-CRM-001/003/007, plus the shared connection, schema, mapping, observation/sync, and health prerequisites before activation. Roll out as an allowlisted pilot with read-only probes, a kill switch, and explicit support matrix. No HubSpot CRM replacement, marketing campaign/sender, consent-law engine, automatic merge, broad bidirectional sync, or plan-independent eligibility claim is included.

Source: https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/legacy-apps/public-apps/overview

## Delivery verification
Add `TestTodo_CONN_CRM_003` as the primary contract test, plus named integration, security, recovery and served-browser cases for the acceptance criteria above. Qualification-only work must prove fail-closed enablement and preserve an explicit go/no-go result. Record exact packages, commands and results in the canonical TODO evidence. Inspect the served setup and health surfaces at desktop, 390 px and 320 px, in en-US, de-DE and Arabic RTL, using existing light/dark themes, keyboard navigation, focus restoration and announced errors. Render-only tests do not replace this browser evidence.

items.title: [PostgreSQL] pgoutput streaming decoder binds tuple values to the wrong columns after any snapshot schema refresh when the publication has a column list
items.body:
## Bug report

With `plugin.name=pgoutput` and a publication created with a per-table **column list**
(`CREATE PUBLICATION p FOR TABLE t (col_a, col_b, ...)`), the first streamed change after
**any** snapshot decodes every tuple value against the wrong column.

If the mis-bound types are incompatible the connector stops with e.g.
`Cannot parse time/date value '3.00', expected format 'y..y-MM-dd HH:mm:ss[.S]X'`.
If they happen to be compatible, **nothing is raised and wrong values are emitted** — a
publication column list can *reorder* as well as subset, so this is a silent-corruption bug
as much as a crash. A connector restart clears it (a new replication session re-sends
RELATION messages); it recurs on the next snapshot.

---

**What Debezium connector do you use and what version?**

`postgresql-connector`, **3.6.0.Final** (run as Debezium Server, `quay.io/debezium/server:3.6.0.Final`, stock image, pristine connector jar).

Verified present unchanged in `v3.6.1.Final` (`PostgresSchema.java`, `PgOutputMessageDecoder.java` and `PostgresSnapshotChangeEventSource.java` are byte-identical to `v3.6.0.Final`) and on `main` — `PostgresSchema.java:91` still reads
`connection.readSchema(tables(), null, null, getTableFilter(), null, true)`.

---

**What is the connector configuration?**

The relevant properties (the rest is transport):

```properties
connector.class=io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector
plugin.name=pgoutput
publication.name=p
publication.autocreate.mode=disabled
snapshot.mode=no_data
signal.enabled.channels=source
topic.prefix=repro
```

---

**What is the captured database version and mode of deployment?**

PostgreSQL 18, local Docker (Debezium Server standalone against a containerised Postgres). Nothing cloud-specific — the defect is purely in the decoder/schema-registry interaction.

---

**What behavior do you expect?**

When the publication publishes a subset (or a reordering) of a table's columns, the streaming
decoder should keep binding tuple values against the column list the RELATION message
described, across snapshots.

---

**What behavior do you see?**

The i-th **published** value is decoded as the i-th **physical** column of the table, from the
first streamed change after a snapshot until the replication session is re-established.

### Why

1. `PgOutputMessageDecoder.handleRelationMessage` (lines 410-411) builds a `Table` from the
   pgoutput RELATION message — i.e. the **publication's** column list — and stores it in the
   shared schema registry via `PostgresSchema.applySchemaChangesForTable(relationId, table)`.
2. `PostgresSchema.refresh(PostgresConnection, boolean)` **line 91** then re-reads every
   captured table over JDBC:
   `connection.readSchema(tables(), null, null, getTableFilter(), null, true)`.
   The 5th argument is the **column filter** and it is hard-coded `null`;
   `JdbcConnection.readTableColumn` (line 1394) treats `null` as "keep everything", so the
   registry entry is overwritten with **every physical column** of the table. The
   relation-derived model is gone.
3. `PgOutputMessageDecoder.resolveRelation` (line 676) → `resolveColumnsFromStreamTupleData`
   (**line 763**) binds the tuple **positionally** against whatever the registry now holds:
   `final io.debezium.relational.Column column = table.columns().get(i);`

Postgres does not re-send a RELATION message merely because the connector re-read
`pg_attribute`, so nothing repairs the binding until the replication session is re-established.

**Both snapshot paths reach step 2:**

* blocking — `PostgresSnapshotChangeEventSource.readTableStructure` (lines 227-235):
  `readSchema(..., null, false)` then `schema.refresh(jdbcConnection, false)`;
* incremental — `PostgresSignalBasedIncrementalSnapshotChangeEventSource.refreshTableSchema`
  → `PostgresSchema.refreshFromIncrementalSnapshot` (line 173) →
  `PostgresSchema.refresh(connection, tableId, …)` (line 125), `null` column filter again.

Two notes that make this wider than it looks:

* An incremental snapshot that exports **zero rows** still poisons the binding —
  `refreshTableSchema` runs before the max-key query.
* Narrowing a signal's `data-collections` does not contain the blast radius:
  `schema.refresh()` re-reads **every** table matching `getTableFilter()`, so a one-table
  snapshot mis-binds all captured tables.

`refreshFromIncrementalSnapshot` already carries the **DBZ-8150** fix, which strips GENERATED
columns during the incremental refresh — the same mechanism with a different trigger. Columns
missing because the publication simply does not publish them were never covered, and nothing in
Debezium reads `pg_publication_tables.attnames`.

Not reachable by configuration, as far as I can tell: `schema.refresh.mode` governs only
whether missing TOASTable data suppresses a refresh
(`skipRefreshSchemaOnMissingToastableData`) and never touches the decoder's binding;
`snapshot.mode.configuration.based.snapshot.schema` does not help because
`RelationalSnapshotChangeEventSource` calls `readTableStructure` unconditionally; and
`publication.autocreate.mode=filtered` "fixes" it only by rewriting the publication without
column lists.

---

**How to reproduce**

Deterministic, 3 steps.

```sql
CREATE TABLE public.orders (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id uuid NOT NULL, software_version varchar,
  order_number varchar, customer_id uuid, store_id uuid, status varchar,
  delivery_date timestamptz, total_amount numeric(12,2), tip numeric(12,2));
ALTER TABLE public.orders REPLICA IDENTITY FULL;
CREATE PUBLICATION p FOR TABLE public.orders
  (id, tenant_id, customer_id, store_id, status, delivery_date, total_amount, tip);
```

The published list's 8th column is `tip` (`numeric`); the table's 8th physical column is
`delivery_date` (`timestamptz`):

```
WAL position (publication column list)      table ordinal (all physical columns)
 1 id                                        1 id                     ok
 2 tenant_id                                 2 tenant_id              ok
 3 customer_id                               3 software_version
 4 store_id                                  4 order_number
 5 status                                    5 customer_id
 6 delivery_date                             6 store_id
 7 total_amount                              7 status
 8 tip           '3.00'  ────────────────►   8 delivery_date  timestamptz   <-- parse failure
```

With the connector configuration above:

1. Start the connector and `INSERT` a row — it decodes correctly.
2. Send an `execute-snapshot` signal, `"type":"blocking"` **or** `"type":"incremental"`.
3. `INSERT` another row →
   `ERROR Cannot parse time/date value '3.00', expected format 'y..y-MM-dd HH:mm:ss[.S]X'`
   and the connector stops.

Measured on the stock `quay.io/debezium/server:3.6.0.Final` image, each round restarting the
connector, writing a control row, running a full snapshot, then writing a row:

| Publication shape | Rounds survived |
|---|---|
| column list | **0 / 5** — every round fails as above |
| column list + the patch below | **5 / 5**, payload fields asserted correct, exactly the published columns present |
| no column list (full row) | **5 / 5** |

Change one type in the table so the shifted values stay parseable and the same rounds emit
**wrong values with no error at all**, which is the case I would flag as the real severity.

---

**Do you see the same behaviour using the latest released Debezium version?**

Yes. `v3.6.1.Final` is byte-identical in the three files involved, and `main` still has the
hard-coded `null` column filter at `PostgresSchema.java:91`.

---

**Suggested fix (validated patch, inline — not submitting a PR)**

Decode against the structure the **stream** described, rather than whatever the shared schema
registry currently holds. A decoder-local map of relation-derived tables is correct regardless
of *why* the two lists differ, which the narrow DBZ-8150 fix is not. This is essentially the
shape SQL Server already settled on in DBZ-2495 / DBZ-2522 (table model derived from the
capture instance's column list).

```diff
--- a/debezium-connector-postgres/src/main/java/io/debezium/connector/postgresql/connection/pgoutput/PgOutputMessageDecoder.java
+++ b/debezium-connector-postgres/src/main/java/io/debezium/connector/postgresql/connection/pgoutput/PgOutputMessageDecoder.java
@@
 import java.util.Collections;
+import java.util.HashMap;
 import java.util.HashSet;
@@
     private final MessageDecoderContext decoderContext;
     private final PostgresConnection connection;
 
+    /**
+     * The table structure of each relation AS THE STREAM DESCRIBES IT, keyed by relation id.
+     * Tuple data is positional against the most recent relation message's column list; the
+     * schema registry is re-read from JDBC without a column filter by paths unrelated to
+     * decoding, after which it carries every column of the table.
+     */
+    private final Map<Integer, Table> relationTables = new HashMap<>();
+
     private Instant commitTimestamp;
@@ handleRelationMessage
         Table table = resolveRelationFromMetadata(new PgOutputRelationMetaData(relationId, schemaName, tableName, columns, primaryKeyColumns));
         decoderContext.getSchema().applySchemaChangesForTable(relationId, table);
+        if (decoderContext.getSchema().tableFor(relationId) != null) {
+            relationTables.put(relationId, table);
+        }
     }
@@ resolveRelation
     private Optional<Table> resolveRelation(int relationId) {
+        final Table relationTable = relationTables.get(relationId);
+        if (relationTable != null) {
+            return Optional.of(relationTable);
+        }
         return Optional.ofNullable(decoderContext.getSchema().tableFor(relationId));
     }
```

A narrower alternative — passing `connectorConfig.getColumnFilter()` instead of `null` at
`PostgresSchema.java:91` and `:125` — repairs the case where `column.include.list` happens to
match the publication, but not a publication column list on its own, which is exactly the
configuration with no other enforcement.

How the patch was validated without a Maven build (the server image ships a full JDK, so the
single file compiles against the jars already present and the class can be swapped into the
connector jar):

```bash
docker cp PgOutputMessageDecoder.java debezium:/tmp/
docker exec debezium sh -lc '
  CP=$(ls /debezium/lib/*.jar | tr "\n" ":")
  /usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk/bin/javac -nowarn -proc:none -cp "$CP" -d /tmp/out /tmp/PgOutputMessageDecoder.java
  cd /tmp/out && /usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk/bin/jar uf \
    /debezium/lib/debezium-connector-postgres-3.6.0.Final.jar \
    $(find io -name "PgOutputMessageDecoder*.class")'
docker restart debezium
```

Happy to rework this into a PR with a test if the approach looks right — filing the report
first since the fix touches the decoder's relationship with the shared schema registry and a
maintainer may prefer a different placement.

---

**Related**

* **DBZ-8150** — same mechanism, GENERATED-columns trigger, fixed narrowly inside
  `refreshFromIncrementalSnapshot`.
* **DBZ-2495 / DBZ-2522** — SQL Server derived its table model from the capture instance's
  column list; that is the shape this needs.
* debezium/dbz#2020 — open sibling report (incremental snapshot, generated column).

items.title: [PP-09B][P0] Assemble canonical ProductionBundle manifests with complete lineage and hashes
items.body:
**Stable key:** PP-09B
**Owner role:** Creative and fulfillment — production maintainer; named implementer and accountable reviewer recorded at kickoff.
**Priority:** P0 — A bundle must prove exactly which approved inputs and output files it contains
**Required for v1:** Yes. **Implementation state:** Planned.

## Current evidence
Live inspection 2026-10-10: main is [24fb18a](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/tree/24fb18a1fc54d34ce71e99a2162d62ebca3a52cd). The complete tracked tree is [README](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/blob/24fb18a1fc54d34ce71e99a2162d62ebca3a52cd/README.md), [OWNERSHIP](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/blob/24fb18a1fc54d34ce71e99a2162d62ebca3a52cd/docs/architecture/OWNERSHIP.md), and [ACCEPTANCE](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/blob/24fb18a1fc54d34ce71e99a2162d62ebca3a52cd/docs/architecture/ACCEPTANCE.md). No AGENTS.md, source, runtime/package manifest, tests or CI exist. #1 is the original WP06 work package; merged [PR #2](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/pull/2) added architecture documentation only. This issue is planned implementation work, not completion evidence.

The [shared catalog](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/blob/main/docs/contract-catalog.md) names ProductionBundle; [shared-contracts #24](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/24) is planned. No canonical executable schema, manifest writer or bundle evidence exists here.

## Scope / non-goals
Build exportArtifactBundle orchestration and getArtifactManifestStatus using canonical ProductionBundle. Join immutable source/template/spec/renderer/font/approval/personalization references, reports and file hashes into the final bundle; atomically publish through storage. Do not invent ProductionArtifactSet or copy shared schemas.

Production owns composition, exact layout/text, templates, personalization, preflight, output storage and manifests. It consumes external approvals and immutable creative/event inputs. Customer identity/order/payment/approval authority, research, GPT Image generation, supplier ordering, pricing and the authoritative ledger remain outside this repository. No paid provider work is authorized.

## Acceptance IDs and expected outcome
Global ART-04 (all files and hashes), ART-05 (asset provenance/approval), with local PP-09B lineage and hashing rules; shared-contracts owns CON-01 schemas.
[Master acceptance definitions](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/integration-evals/blob/ff1f6d2df816ebbff34742f51be728fcb5c28cb5/planning/acceptance-checklist.md) and [JSON evidence tracker](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/integration-evals/blob/ff1f6d2df816ebbff34742f51be728fcb5c28cb5/planning/acceptance-checklist.json) retain their existing global IDs, priorities and owner roles. This run does not change that tracker.

- [ ] PP-09B.1: Manifest carries schema and bundle ID/revision, tenant/project-safe scope, design/artwork/approval/fact refs and hashes, composition revision, product/template/spec identity, renderer/tool/font versions, exact formatting/repair policy, source lineage and personalization row/batch scope. Preserve privacy through scoped refs/digests rather than unneeded raw attendee values.
- [ ] PP-09B.2: List every shipped file with safe relative path, media type, byte length, SHA-256, dimensions/units/DPI/profile and raster/vector characteristics. Include final preflight rule/report refs, warnings/errors/information and explicit passed/failed/unsupported/unknown state; presence of files alone is not readiness.
- [ ] PP-09B.3: Hash protocol is unambiguous: hash payload files first; canonicalize manifest without its own digest or final ZIP hash; compute detached manifest digest; package payloads plus manifest; compute final ZIP digest in detached metadata/status. No self-hash recursion or omitted/unlisted payloads. Canonical shared hashing rules win after review.
- [ ] PP-09B.4: Keep source-artwork, preview, composed-output, manifest and bundle hashes distinct. Changed composition/personalization/spec produces a new identity and cannot reuse an unrelated approval or downstream purchase authorization.
- [ ] PP-09B.5: Only complete output sets with passing mandatory checks and current permission applicability are published eligible. Retrieval distinguishes processing/failed/partial/completed and readiness; validate every stored reference and hash without starting new exports.
- [ ] PP-09B.6: Provide a verification command that consumes an existing bundle/manifest, validates canonical schema, recomputes all hashes, rejects extra/missing/tampered files and reports typed errors. Read-only verification cannot count as a new production attempt.

## Approach and migration implications
Consume accepted schema/types from PP-01B and SC-07C. Assemble file hashes after export, produce canonical manifest bytes, ask PP-09A's packager for ZIP, then publish via PP-10A. Cross-reference exact operation/trace/evidence IDs without pricing or authority claims. Maintain supported-old-schema read fixtures and explicit migrations that preserve old immutable manifests.

## Relationships
**Parent:** #1 (WP06 / PP-EPIC).
**Blocked by:** #10 (storage), #15 (exporters); [shared-contracts #24](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/24), [#8](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/8)
**Blocks:** #3 (PP-12 release gate); downstream edges are maintained in #1's dependency and coverage map.
**Related:** [fulfillment-connectors #1](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/1), [shared-contracts #29](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/29).

## Executable validation
Required implementation commands; these do not exist and were not run during backlog triage. PP-01A must establish the dispatcher and fail on unknown/missing suites. Run in a clean pinned checkout with no provider credentials.

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
npm run verify -- --suite manifests --mode offline --evidence-dir out/evidence
```

Produce a complete bundle, validate shared schema, unpack it and recompute every file/manifest/ZIP hash with an independent verifier. Alter/remove/add one file, change product units/spec and present stale approval; assert failures. Fetch completed status twice and prove identical immutable refs with no new render/export attempt.

## Required evidence for closure
Attach canonical contract pin, sample manifest/bundle/detached metadata, hash-protocol specification, lineage graph and independent pass/tamper/missing/extra-file verification reports. Include merged implementation SHA, exact runtime/dependency/shared-contracts pins, fixture digests, command/exit-code logs and sanitized durable evidence links. Record limitations and reviewer sign-off. No unchecked criterion or missing dependency evidence is complete; documentation/mocks alone do not verify global end-to-end criteria.


## Production & commerce cross-repository audit correction — 2026-10-10

**Single accountable artifact owner:** PP-09B / this issue (#16) owns the published canonical ProductionBundle and the all-file/manifest/bundle hash evidence for ART-04. PP-07 (#11) owns preflight findings and PP-09A (#15) owns renderer/export file production; both feed their verified results and files into this issue. PP-12F (#19) owns integration-corpus orchestration, not ART-04 acceptance ownership. No artifact is eligible for handoff until this issue publishes and independently verifies the actual canonical bundle.

**Required downstream dependency chain:** print-production #11 and #15 → this issue (#16) publishes the actual ProductionBundle → [fulfillment-connectors #10](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/10) validates that actual bundle and unchanged hashes with its real offline consumer validator → print-production #19 runs the pinned integration fixtures against that accepted validator result → print-production #3 applies the release gate. A proposed manifest, local mock, or absent validator is a blocker; fulfillment sandbox/live order evidence remains separately owned and is not required by the offline production gate.

**PP-09B closure evidence:** close #16 when this producer has attached the actual published canonical ProductionBundle and manifest with pinned source/schema/tool revisions, complete payload and manifest hash inventory, PP-09B command and exit logs, independent pass/tamper/missing/extra-file verification output, and reviewer sign-off. The fulfillment-connectors #10 unchanged-hash offline consumer result is downstream evidence: PP-12F #19 collects and pins it, and PP-12 #3 assesses it. That downstream validator result is not a prerequisite for closing this producer issue.

**Audit state:** backlog prepared only; PP-09B implementation and its own closure evidence remain pending. Keep #16 open until its producer evidence above is attached. The deliverable sequence remains actual #16 bundle → fulfillment #10 real offline validator → PP #19 → PP #3.

## Triage section index (2026-10-10)
_Added by org triage. No existing text above was changed. This maps the org-standard sections to the sections already in this issue._

- **Context:** see *Current evidence* above.
- **Scope / Non-goals:** see *Scope / non-goals* above.
- **Acceptance criteria:** see the checkbox list under *Acceptance IDs and expected outcome* above.
- **Evidence required:** see *Required evidence for closure* above.

### Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts#24, Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts#8, Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production#10, Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production#15

## CURRENT CHARTER — Shared-phase six-chat system (2026-10-11)

**Worker identity:** Chat 2 · **GitHub journal:** #22 · **Current GLOBAL phase:** `DATABASE` (entire LMS DB00–DB10 for ALL six chats).

**This issue no longer owns a permanent product domain.** The user replaced the former domain-per-chat model with **six interchangeable workers in one global phase**. Do **not** follow the historical body below for task ownership. The **source of truth** is:
- [Six-chat v2 operating system](https://github.com/42Students/lms-vnext/blob/main/docs/coordination/six-chat-operating-system.md)
- [Global phase state](https://github.com/42Students/lms-vnext/blob/main/docs/coordination/phase-state.json)
- [Shared work queue](https://github.com/42Students/lms-vnext/blob/main/docs/coordination/work-queue.json)
- [Worker 2 checkpoint](https://github.com/42Students/lms-vnext/blob/main/docs/coordination/lanes/chat-02.json)

**Resume:** `Continue chat 2 work` means fetch fresh `main`, oracles, state, queue, checkpoint and issue comments; resume claimed task or CAS-claim next eligible **DATABASE** task, regardless of domain. When task is done or blocked, release/mark it with real evidence, then claim next task **in DATABASE**, never skip to API individually. If no eligible task, review/unblock or document a genuine missing DB task without stealing another worker's claim. The global DATABASE→API transition occurs only when **all** database phase gates have independently passing evidence and the complete next-phase inventory is ready.

**Technical single-writer exception:** Chat 1 remains exclusive numbered Drizzle migration/schema-barrel/CI integrator; this does **not** assign DB00–DB04 exclusively to Chat 1. Other chats can work on any DB package and stage migration drafts.

**Status:** `Chat 2 stats` reports **worker task history**, tests and current global phase, not domain percent. Tests authored are not tests passed. Use this issue for current work/checkpoints and handoffs. The previous domain assignment body below is archived for reference only.

---

<summary>Historical pre-2026-10-11 domain-specific assignment — obsolete, not operative</summary>

items.body:
# Lion BI / Lola — Pass 5 completion coordination (staging only)

**Objective:** deliver an accurate, permission-safe, reliable daily operating system, not a page-count milestone. Platform: Lion BI; assistant: Lola. No production or LYO changes.

## Parallel agent task board
- **Agent A — Reliability and data refresh / P0:** #115
- **Agent B — QuickBooks + Outlook integration correctness:** #116
- **Agent C — Lola cross-department business journeys:** #117
- **Agent D — premium orb, voice and unified UX:** #118
- **Agent E — launch ops/billing/onboarding/recovery:** #119
- **Agent QA — independent DEBUG, security, regression, fix verification:** #114 (mandatory independent check on every PR)

## Integration model
1. Each agent branches from `integrate/pass4-staging-20261111` and submits a **draft PR targeting that branch**. Avoid shared branches and merge commits.
2. Ownership: A — refresh/worker; B — QBO/Outlook connector; C — Lola workflow API & provenance; D — frontend/orb/voice; E — launch operational tests/docs; QA — independent regression suite and security verification.
3. Shared API/schema changes require an interface contract in the originating PR, tests, and a coordination comment on this board before implementation.
4. Independent QA reviews each workstream with P0/P1 defects, failing tests, and regression fixes. No approval by an agent for its own change.
5. Integrate only after all branch CI passes, no P0/P1 remains, RBAC + cross-tenant negative tests pass, and three failure/retry exercises pass (external unknown outcome, sync outage, receipt replay).
6. Deploy **staging only** after approval and record SHAs for web/backend/worker/cron. No auto-merge, no production deployment.

## Evidence-required release gates
**G0 Stability:** failed snapshot job fixed, logs include actionable root cause without PII, freshness timestamps accurate; full backend/web/worker release SHA compatibility.

**G1 Connectors:** sandbox verified QuickBooks refresh + balance reconciliation and Outlook OAuth/read/threaded send/confirmation. All unavailable real-account tests shown as unverified.

**G2 Journeys:** executive, finance/AR, sales/inventory, warehouse receipt/damage claim and pricing/AP journeys have traced records, permissions and recovery testing.

**G3 Lola:** no redundant nested mini chat; premium untouched approved orb, touch/mic/output responsiveness or honest browser fallback, user-selected English/Spanish, mobile/desktop acceptance.

**G4 Launch:** onboarding and role gates, test billing lifecycle, backups + restore exercise, alerts, incident workflow, staff pilot and rollback.

**G5 Independent signoff:** debug agent reports all critical defects, tests + evidence, and gives explicit NO-GO until all other gates are proven.

## Initial live evidence (2026-11-12 Eastern)
- Railway project `SecretaryAI-Staging` environment `staging`; web/backend/Redis/dashboard worker running.
- `LionBI-Staging-Readonly-Snapshot-Cron` latest deployment `e1bc5c5a-0cf9-4059-b8d8-fae4cff6ed4c` CRASHED; latest log only says `failed at stage=read_and_refresh_dashboard`.
- Web is attached to `feat/staging-lionbi-lola-centered-home-20261111`; backend and worker still source `feat/staging-secure-manager-invites-20261108`. Keep version compatibility explicit.
- Existing UI PR #113; security/approval PR #108; other ongoing features #105/#103. Reuse work; no duplicated implementation.

## Execution status and blockers
Creating issues and mentioning @copilot does NOT prove an autonomous agent started. GitHub's issue assignee API currently returns HTTP 403 for `copilot-swe-agent[bot]` under the connected account, so direct dispatch is **not confirmed**. Railway Cloud Agents feature was enabled, but Railway Automations is unavailable on this account and the connected Railway tools cannot start a cloud-agent task. Treat all six tasks as **prepared / awaiting confirmed agent launch** until PRs or task IDs exist.

**Never call the system fully ready based solely on code committed or unit tests.**

items.title: Integration: build typed Connector SDK, capability adapters, and MCP gateway boundary
items.body:
Parent epic: #1
Depends on: #9, #14, #22, and #28
Supports: #10, #17, #21, and future private connectors

## Objective
Build the domain-neutral Connector SDK and gateway layer that exposes typed System-of-Record capabilities to governed workflows while keeping MCP/tool discovery separate from identity, authorization, transactions, idempotency, compensation, audit, and tenant policy.

## Shared execution procedure

Canonical source: `ed3c/skills-shared@ec5a240fa3cbafda2c6a8bce0ae12143e0992f80`; all Skill bodies remain exclusively there.

Applicable paths:
- `skills/agentic-tech-lead-orchestration/SKILL.md`
- `skills/spatial-loop-systems-engineering/SKILL.md`
- `skills/spatial-loop-systems-engineering/references/architecture-watch-loop.md`
- `skills/procedural-shadow-runtime/SKILL.md`
- `skills/git-town-stacked-pr-worker/SKILL.md`
- `skills/dual-forge-repository-loop/SKILL.md`

Procedure delta: PRECHECK every external side-effect and trust boundary; lock typed connector/capability contracts; model timeout-after-unknown-completion, rate limit, partial success, retry, compensation, credential expiry, and schema drift; require exact receipts and negative controls. Shared Skill bodies remain external.

## Required capability contract
- connector/system/version identity;
- tenant and credential reference, never credential value;
- operation/action class;
- request/response schemas;
- side-effect and reversibility class;
- idempotency support and operation key;
- transaction/atomicity boundary;
- compensation/rollback support;
- timeout/rate-limit/retry policy;
- sandbox/dry-run support;
- approval/policy requirements;
- data classification, region, and retention constraints;
- audit and postcondition observer.

## Required adapters
Provide synthetic in-memory or containerized contract-test adapters for representative ERP/CRM/WMS/ticketing behavior. Product-specific live credentials and tenant mappings remain private.

## Hard invariants
- MCP is a capability/tool protocol surface, not the authorization or transaction boundary.
- Token passthrough, ambient authority, arbitrary endpoint selection, and model-selected credentials are forbidden.
- A connector cannot expose or execute capability beyond the compiled DigitalEmployeeSpec and current policy decision.
- Unknown completion enters observation/reconciliation; it is never blindly retried.
- Irreversible or unsupported-compensation operations cannot be autonomous.
- Connector schemas, behavior, and evidence remain exact-version specific.
- Public adapters use synthetic data; customer-specific mappings stay in the private forge.

## Required evidence
Connector conformance suite; duplicate request, timeout-after-commit, partial success, rate limit, schema drift, credential revocation, audience mismatch, policy denial, unsupported compensation, cross-tenant, SSRF/endpoint allowlist, and audit omission controls; typed connector receipts.

## Non-goals
No live NetSuite/SAP/Salesforce credential, no customer mapping, no production MCP exposure, no autonomous financial commit, and no copied Skill body.

## Evidence ceiling
Synthetic connector integration may reach L3. Real provider behavior, production credentials, rate limits, transaction guarantees, and customer acceptance require private/live evidence.

## Suggested branch
`agent/connector-sdk-mcp-gateway` after #9/#22/#28 contracts are admitted.

items.title: Hardening, security and release readiness
items.body:
## Scope
Close the security, operational and release-readiness gaps before any controlled pilot or production claim.

## Current verified baseline
- Initial threat model, data/tenancy architecture, CI quality checks, PostgreSQL RLS integration workflow and CodeQL workflow exist.
- The threat model explicitly lists formal data-flow diagrams, per-domain STRIDE review, DPIA where required, penetration testing, incident runbooks, recovery objectives and verified restoration evidence as production prerequisites.
- Current connector visibility does not establish Dependabot alert, code-scanning alert, dependency-graph/SBOM or branch-protection status. These must be verified in GitHub by an authorized administrator or an available API.

## Acceptance criteria
- Produce and review data-flow diagrams and STRIDE threat assessments for identity, marketplace, communication, projects, trust, financial ledger, AI and integrations.
- Complete privacy/legal review and DPIA where applicable for launch jurisdictions and sensitive processing.
- Verify dependency alerts, code-scanning findings, secret scanning, SBOM/provenance and remediation evidence; record inaccessible checks as unverified, not clean.
- Confirm branch protection/rulesets require the intended review and passing CI gates; do not weaken repository protections to unblock work.
- Add operational runbooks for incidents, access revocation, key rotation, backups, restore, data retention/deletion and support escalation.
- Demonstrate backup restoration against documented RPO/RTO; record evidence and owners.
- Complete independent penetration testing, accessibility audit, load/reliability checks and pilot-readiness review with tracked findings.
- Keep launch blocked while critical security findings, legal decisions or required operational evidence remain open.

## Dependencies
This is an exit gate across #34–#37 and #39. A green CI run is necessary but does not by itself establish security or production readiness.
