items.body:
Each claim below was flagged by the claim audit: a part of its statement, in **bold** where it can be marked, that its judges did not find any quote stating. Borderline claims (unmarked) had only low-confidence flags, about half of them real; *(overreach)* claims had a confident one. Each link opens the claim in its subject file, with its `evidence` quotes and any `conditions` just below; the rule is [the audit rubric](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/_meta/evals/claim-audit/rubric.md): every material part of the statement must be stated by a quote (an absence may rest on the search its conditions record). Tick a claim that is fine as written. Comment with the claim ID and what to change for one to narrow or to quote; it gets fixed in a pull request. Links are at commit f12f6274. These claims were flagged in only one of two full audit runs (2026-11-03). An Opus review of the claims flagged in both runs (#313 to #323) found almost all of them needed a change, so these get the same review.

- [ ] [`shared.admin-rbac.zpa:feature-list`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.admin-rbac.zpa.json#L73) **A Private Access admin role** enables access per feature, chosen from these features: **Administration Control**, **API Key Management**, App Connector Management, Authentication, Business Continuity Management, B2B Exchange, **Certificate Management**, Client Connector Portal, Client Sessions, Cloud Connector Management, **Company Information**, Configuration, Dashboard, Diagnostics, Log Streaming, Machine Management, Notification Management, **Policies**, Private Service Edge Management, Privileged Remote Access, Privileged Sessions, Security Management, SCIM Management and VPN (For Legacy Apps). Each grants Full or Read Only access, except Client Connector Portal (Full) and Dashboard (Read Only).
- [x] [`shared.audit-logs:cbc-audit-report`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.audit-logs.json#L160) The Cloud & Branch Connector API has an **asynchronous** audit report: POST /auditlogEntryReport starts a CSV export, GET reports its status, DELETE cancels it, and GET /auditlogEntryReport/download returns the CSV data.
- [ ] [`shared.cloud-architecture.central-authority:heartbeat`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.cloud-architecture.central-authority.json#L186) **The Zscaler cloud heartbeats every second**, so all nodes learn of a policy change; any Public Service Edge can pull the changed policy when it sees a new request from the organization, so users get the new policy when they next connect, wherever they are.
- [ ] [`shared.cloud-architecture.cloud-names:derived-names`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.cloud-architecture.cloud-names.json#L154) The Zscaler Client Connector and Cloud & Branch Connector clouds follow the organization's Internet & SaaS cloud: a tenant on `zscaler.net` uses `mobile.zscaler.net` for Client Connector and `connector.zscaler.net` for Cloud & Branch Connector, and **each of the five Internet & SaaS clouds has a `mobile.` and a `connector.` counterpart**.
- [ ] [`shared.cloud-architecture.tunnels:edges-manage-mtunnels`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.cloud-architecture.tunnels.json#L69) Public and Private Service Edges create and manage Microtunnels, including authentication, policy, setup, teardown and data forwarding; **M-Tunnels are end-to-end encrypted connections designed to keep all traffic separate**.
- [x] [`shared.cloud-architecture:three-components`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.cloud-architecture.json#L107) Zscaler describes **its Internet & SaaS cloud infrastructure** as three key components: the Central Authority, the Public Service Edges for Internet & SaaS, and Nanolog clusters.
- [ ] [`shared.event-monitoring.channels:channel-list`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.event-monitoring.channels.json#L114) GET /subscriptions/channels lists the channel types supported for the tenant, **each with `type`, `description` and `setup_required`**; SNS shows `setup_required: true`, meaning more configuration is needed before it can be used.
- [ ] [`shared.log-export.zdx:webhooks`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.log-export.zdx.json#L132) ****The ZDX ranges** list** Webhooks as not supported on Standard, 10 on Microsoft 365 and Advanced, and 50 on Advanced Plus.
- [ ] [`shared.mcp-server:lock-resolution`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.mcp-server.json#L128) The MCP tree's generated requirements resolve `mcp==2.0.0` and `zscaler-sdk-python==1.9.43`, while **the Python SDK vendored in this repository** is version 1.11.3; the lock file's own editable entry for `zscaler-mcp` still says 0.15.3.
- [ ] [`shared.oneapi.rate-limits:go-client-limiters`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.oneapi.rate-limits.json#L304) The Go SDK's OneAPI client throttles on the client side with a limiter per service: ZIA and ZTW, each at 20 GET and 10 POST/PUT/DELETE calls per 10 seconds. At v3.8.55 both had hourly caps of 950 GET, 950 POST/PUT and 380 DELETE per method; at v3.8.58 ZIA's hourly caps are per endpoint (method plus path, IDs normalized) at 950 GET, 380 POST/PUT and 380 DELETE, while ZTW keeps the per-method 950, 950 and 380. ZPA has 20 GET and 10 POST/PUT/DELETE calls per 10 seconds; ZCC 100 calls per hour and 3 per day for downloadDevices; and **a default limiter covers other paths**.
- [ ] [`shared.pac-files.syntax:pse-ports`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.pac-files.syntax.json#L152) Public Service Edges accept web requests on ports 80, 443, 9400, 9443 and 9480. Port 9400 is an alternative when a host on the path redirects traffic before it reaches the Service Edge, and should only be returned if it is open outbound; 9443 is for remote users whose HTTPS the service should proxy and inspect; 9480 exempts traffic from a known location from authentication, while **remote users on it are still forced to authenticate**.
- [x] [`shared.pac-files.syntax:regex-cost`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.pac-files.syntax.json#L261) **Regular expressions are allowed** but should be minimized and kept efficient; complex ones used to make a file smaller can make it less efficient.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-go.cache:prefix-invalidation-over-broad`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-go.cache.json#L260) Invalidation matches cache keys by raw string prefix, and a write's parent key is its URL cut at the last `/`, so a create on a top-level collection such as `/zia/api/v1/firewallFilteringRules` clears every cached read under `/zia/api/v1`. **Up to v3.8.57 the match only deletes entries**; from v3.8.58 the same prefixes are also registered with the write tracker, which matches them by raw string prefix too.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-go.cache:two-owners-possible`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-go.cache.json#L138) Claiming a URL as in flight is a separate check and store rather than one atomic step, so **two GETs that miss the cache at the same moment can both send the request**.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:zcc-v1-stops-on-page-shorter-than-requested`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-go.list-pagination.json#L91) The **ZCC v1** list helper (`ReadAllPages`) clamps the page size (0 or less becomes 50, more than 5000 becomes 5000), starts at page 1 and stops at the first page with fewer items than it asked for; the device list calls it with a page size of 1000.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:zia-posture-import-by-name-uses-list-helper`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-go.list-pagination.json#L730) Importing a ZCC ZIA posture profile by a non-numeric ID calls `GetByName`, which fetches the list through the v2 paging helper and compares names client-side. **A numeric ID imports without any list call**.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-go.request-handling:rate-and-timeout-options-rebuild-clients`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-go.request-handling.json#L207) `WithRequestTimeout`, `WithRateLimitMaxRetries`, `WithRateLimitMinWait`, `WithRateLimitMaxWait` and `WithRateLimitRemainingThreshold` each call `setHttpClients` again, **building fresh clients from the configuration as it stands at that moment**.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-go.retries:default-retries-connection-errors`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-go.retries.json#L118) **The retryablehttp default** retries most transport errors (anything except redirect, scheme, header, and certificate failures), 429, and 500-range responses other than 501.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-go.retries:provider-sdk-pins`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-go.retries.json#L265) Which SDK each audited provider build carries decides whether it has the v3.8.43 fix: ZIA provider 4.8.3 uses v3.8.44 (fixed); ZPA 4.4.10 uses v3.8.42, ZCC 0.1.0-beta.1 uses v3.8.37, and ZTC 0.2.0 uses v3.8.40 (all before the fix). **ZTC 0.2.0 is still the pinned ZTC release**.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-go.retries:retry-policy-ignores-method`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-go.retries.json#L58) *(overreach)* The SDK's OneAPI client decides whether to retry from the response or error only, **never from the HTTP method**: its policy retries configured status codes and edit-lock conflicts, then defers to the retryablehttp default. From v3.8.43 it also stops retrying a 5xx that carries a deterministic API verdict; before that, every 5xx except 501 was retried.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-go.zero-value-writes:zcc-writes-marshal-caller-struct`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-go.zero-value-writes.json#L242) ****Client Connector (ZCC) writes serialize the caller's struct** directly with `json.Marshal`**.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-python.errors:api-error-object`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-python.errors.json#L32) A non-2xx REST response is turned into a `ZscalerAPIError` built from the URL, the response and the parsed body, and **the request executor hands it back in the error slot**. A response whose Content-Type is JSON but whose body does not parse is returned as an `HTTPError` carrying the status code and body text.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-python.pagination:next-empty-page`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-python.pagination.json#L51) `next()` **raises StopIteration only when `has_next()` is already false**; when the page it fetches is empty it returns None with no error instead.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-python.request-handling:body-camel-case`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-python.request-handling.json#L38) **For a dictionary request body**, the request executor camel-cases the keys with `convert_keys_to_camel_case`, except on the ZDX and ZTB legacy clients and on endpoints containing `/zdx/`, `/easm/` or `/ztb/`, whose bodies it sends as given. For `/zcc/` it converts selectively, leaving `WebPolicy.SNAKE_CASE_KEYS` as they are, and a body the ZCC serializer already produced (`_ZccWireBody`) is sent unchanged.
- [ ] [`shared.sdk-python.response-handling:status-accessor`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.sdk-python.response-handling.json#L77) `ZscalerAPIResponse` keeps the HTTP status in `_status`, reads it from the underlying response **once** in its constructor, and **exposes it through `get_status()`**.
- [x] [`shared.secret-surfaces.withheld:zid-secret-create`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.secret-surfaces.withheld.json#L178) POST /api-clients/{id}/secrets creates a new secret for the client, **with no masking note in its description**, and its 201 response requires `id`, `createdAt` and `value`, described as the secret value.
- [ ] [`shared.terminology.service-edge-names:virtual-zen-api`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.terminology.service-edge-names.json#L89) The ZIA API lists and adds Virtual Service Edge clusters at /virtualZenClusters and Virtual Service Edges at /virtualZenNodes.
- [ ] [`shared.terraform.credential-handling:c2c-ir-entity-log-includes-secrets`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.terraform.credential-handling.json#L178) The same data source logs `resp.OnboardableEntity` with `%+v`. That value is a pointer to a struct that holds `TenantAuthorizationInfo` by value, whose string members include `ClientSecret`, `SecretToken` and `UserPwd`, **so the formatted line prints the secret-bearing members' contents**. The line is prefixed `[DEBUG]` and **has no redaction**.
- [ ] [`shared.terraform.credential-handling:zia-psk-handled-differently`](https://github.com/dvmrry/zscaler-skill/blob/f12f62746e8572fc7a1e7762189dcf35c384afd4/references/shared/shared.terraform.credential-handling.json#L332) The ZIA data sources are not uniform. In `zia_location_management` the nested `pre_shared_key` is marked `Sensitive: true`. In `zia_traffic_forwarding_vpn_credentials` the `Sensitive: true` line is commented out, and so is the line that would set `pre_shared_key` from the response, so that data source declares the attribute but **does not populate it**.

**MVP 2: 継続業務・端末連携** — 継続業務/端末連携の採用時に必要部分だけ実装。製品scopeは #611、全体の依存/選定は #460。

## Goal
Define a shared EvidenceRef schema so Suisui outputs can cite original sources across QZT containers, KnowledgeBase RAG results, local files, meetings, tasks, and execution receipts.

## Why
Suisui's Business value depends on trusted, source-backed automation. Users must see why a task, meeting brief, or connector draft was generated, and companies need auditability.

## Scope
- EvidenceRef fields: source system, tenant/workspace id, document id, container id, byte/line range, checksum, title, redacted preview, access policy, citation URL if available.
- QZT evidence range conventions.
- KnowledgeBase citation mapping.
- Local document/task/meeting/receipt source mapping.
- Validation and redaction rules.
- Display rules in Assistant Queue, meeting briefs, project memory, and receipts.

## Acceptance criteria
- Suisui can store and render evidence refs without storing raw document bodies in sync plaintext.
- QZT range refs and KnowledgeBase citation refs share one display abstraction.
- Evidence refs survive generated draft -> approval -> execution receipt flow.
- Tests cover schema validation, checksum presence, redaction, tenant scope, and invalid ref denial.

items.title: Adopt PostgreSQL for shared multi-instance persistence
items.body:
## Context

Today Kernector uses **SQLite** for the document catalog (`DOCUMENT_CATALOG_SQL_PATH`) and JSON files for Google Drive OAuth. That is correct for single-process local deploys. It is **not** suitable as the system of record when multiple app replicas must share catalog, membership, and connector grants.

Config currently rejects `DOCUMENT_CATALOG_BACKEND=postgres`. There is no ADR selecting a networked database.

## Goal

Adopt **PostgreSQL** as the shared persistence backend for multi-instance deployments, with an ADR and a composition/config path that can target Postgres for catalog (and related tenancy tables).

## Scope

* Write an ADR: PostgreSQL for shared multi-instance persistence (when required); SQLite remains allowed for single-host.
* Add config/composition wiring for Postgres (connection URL, migrations approach, health checks).
* Provide a `DocumentCatalog` (and later grant/membership) adapter path on Postgres, or a clear migration plan from the SQLite schema.
* Document local/dev vs shared-deploy settings in README / ARCHITECTURE.

## Out of scope

* Forcing every local developer onto Postgres
* Full cutover of production data and multi-instance leakage suite (— sibling story **Multi-instance shared persistence…**, which is **blocked by this ticket**)
* Changing Chroma / vector store technology

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Accepted ADR records Postgres as the shared DB for multi-instance multi-tenant claims
- [ ] Settings can select Postgres without breaking SQLite single-host path (or deprecation is explicit and documented)
- [ ] Schema migrations run safely against Postgres
- [ ] Smoke tests prove catalog (and any landed tenancy tables) work on Postgres
- [ ] README / ARCHITECTURE describe when to use SQLite vs Postgres

## NOTE — tickets blocked by this story

Any work that **requires** a networked shared database or claims **multi-instance multi-tenant** deployment must wait on this issue, including:

* **Multi-instance shared persistence for catalog, membership, and connector grants** (sibling under #257) — **blocked by this ticket**
* Do **not** treat SQLite-only Drive grant scoping as multi-replica ready

## Parent

Sub-issue of [#257](https://github.com/mahmoudazaid/Kernector/issues/257) Epic: Project Workspaces and Authorization.

items.title: Epic: Evidence-grounded memory pipeline and maintained project briefs
items.body:
## Goal

Turn the Hindsight research into a measured, evidence-grounded Continuum roadmap without replacing Continuum's stronger lifecycle/security model or duplicating Engram's code intelligence.

Source: [Hindsight research report](https://github.com/nucleoid/openclaw-workspace/blob/main/second-brain/projects/hindsight-continuum-research-2026-10-16.md), based on `vectorize-io/hindsight@9a499b1759084a86598eff8af30ed59f7354e76c` and Continuum baseline `51fe3a8b9a133fac1969e282fcc08a3aadd96525`.

## Architecture boundary

- **Engram owns code-only architecture intelligence:** implemented symbols, flows, dependencies, contracts, and change impact.
- **Continuum owns memory semantics:** decisions, rationale, constraints, rejected alternatives, supersession, provenance, authorization, and lifecycle.
- Maintained project briefs are thin, source-neutral synthesis over authorized evidence. They distinguish implemented facts, recorded intent, and inference; cite source-memory versions and repository commit/index freshness; surface contradictions; and invalidate/refresh affected sections.
- Engram is optional. Continuum keeps full non-code utility. No Engram API is assumed.
- Continuum scope authorization never grants repository evidence access. Every stage requires the intersection of caller authority, source/assertion authority, connector authority, and residency/provider policy.

## Child work (dependency order)

- [ ] #25 — evaluation corpus and ablation harness
- [ ] #26 — assertion/source authorization and threat model (depends on #25)
- [ ] #27 — versioned evidence DAG, quarantine, and erasure (depends on #26)
- [ ] #28 — serialized context/output/deadline/spend budgets (depends on #25, #26)
- [ ] #29 — pre-final-cut reranking (depends on #25, #26, #28)
- [ ] #30 — optional source-preserving extraction (depends on #25–#28)
- [ ] #31 — event time, ingestion time, TTL, hard filters, and ranking hints (depends on #25, #27)
- [ ] #32 — optional source-neutral Engram connector/query receipts (depends on #26–#28)
- [ ] #33 — scoped maintained briefs (depends on #25–#31; #32 optional)
- [ ] #34 — bounded typed relationship expansion, only if measured (depends on #25–#29 foundations)

## Cross-cutting acceptance criteria

- Evaluation covers retrieval, extraction, synthesis, security, temporal/supersession/deletion behavior, latency, and spend with ablations and frozen fixtures.
- Persistent derivatives use versioned evidence dependencies and are synchronously quarantined after source deletion, revocation, or material change; asynchronous repair never leaves stale prose readable.
- Source-document and extracted-assertion authorization remain separate through extraction, reranking, source expansion, synthesis, cache/history/export, and optional connectors.
- Prompt injection and untrusted-source threats, repeated-source non-independence, failures/fallbacks, provider/local-only controls, resource ceilings, audit, Entra/ACL/offboarding, and erasure are explicit.
- Explicit decision supersession remains authoritative. Deterministic `AGENTS.md` output remains a separate trustworthy reference, not an LLM-maintained brief.

## Non-goals

- Replacing Continuum with Hindsight or adopting Hindsight as a backend.
- Making personality/agent dispositions the default memory model.
- Prompt-based declassification, tags as an ACL substitute, or proof count as truth probability.
- Duplicating Engram's code graph or inventing Engram APIs.
- Building a general relationship graph before measured benefit.
- Deployment, migration, infrastructure changes, or production rollout under this planning epic.

Related existing delivery work: #18, #19, #20, #21. Those issues cover transport, packaging, deployment, and UAT rather than this memory-architecture roadmap.

items.body:
# P2 — Managed runtime and MCP

Parent specification and coordination: https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/5

Status: ready for manager decomposition after assignment. No implementation, paid experiments or rollout dispatched by this issue.

## Problem Statement

A smart model cannot by itself preserve decisions, enforce authority or reliably resume management work. Separate UI and assistant implementations could fork plans or bypass checks.

## Solution

Run bounded management tasks over Relay's existing authenticated services, durable plans and execution records. Expose the same governed operations to the native experience and MCP.

## User Stories

1. As an artist, I want to have my goals and explicit preferences remembered, so that I do not repeat my brief every session.
2. As an artist, I want to inspect and correct inferred preferences, so that Relay does not silently impose assumptions.
3. As an artist, I want to resume a manager task after interruption, so that my previous decisions remain intact.
4. As an artist, I want to use an external assistant on the same plan, so that I do not create conflicting schedules.
5. As an artist, I want to receive a truthful limited result during model failure, so that I can distinguish saved work from unfinished reasoning.
6. As an artist, I want to cancel a manager task, so that it stops preparing new work within my revoked scope.
7. As an artist, I want to have permission checked on every action, so that a prompt cannot grant access to another account.
8. As an operator, I want to bound calls, time and spend per task, so that background work cannot run indefinitely.
9. As an operator, I want to identify the model configuration and evidence for a plan, so that I can investigate problems and roll back changes.
10. As a manager agent, I want to reuse established plan and execution authorities, so that parallel implementation does not create competing state.

## Implementation Decisions

- Own runtime orchestration, brief persistence semantics, authenticated management operations and the MCP adapter. Experience owns presentation; execution owns delivery; evidence owns metric calculations.
- Inventory general AI, gallery-editor and conversational-planning provider paths before selecting existing ownership. Reuse Goal Cycle and conversational-plan revisions/checkpoints rather than create another plan engine.
- Use bounded fact loading, gap handling, proposal, validation, review, execution delegation and assessment with durable stopping/error states. Scheduled triggers initiate bounded runs; the process need not remain continuously reasoning.
- Define a versioned context/result envelope with creator identity, brief, asset references, capabilities, evidence, plan revision, allowed result types, cancellation and budget. Application identity and approval evidence cannot be supplied as trusted model assertions.
- MCP remains a thin authenticated adapter over the same operations. Verify scoped reads as well as writes. Planning approval must not grant external publishing authority.
- Keep imported text and tool content untrusted. Avoid credentials and unnecessary raw patron/source content in model context or traces.
- Recheck current revision, authorization and cancellation before mutations. Replay returns saved results; retries do not regenerate approved payloads.
- Configuration promotion is explicit and reversible after P3 evidence; old evaluation budgets or provider choices do not authorize new paid runs.

## Testing Decisions

- Primary seam: authenticated management operations through real services and isolated database state, including prepare, revise, preview, approval, cancellation and resumed status.
- Reuse conversational-planning API restart/replay/concurrency and tenant-isolation cases, Goal Cycle checkpoints and gallery-editor stale-change/budget tests.
- Thin native/MCP parity tests prove equivalent authorization and resulting records; arbitrary MCP requests cannot bypass service rules.
- Provider-adapter tests cover budget exhaustion, timeout, malformed output, injection attempts and cancellation without fabricated completion.

## Out of Scope

A second scheduler/library/permission ledger, custom model training, general-purpose agent framework, unauthenticated MCP access, unattended publishing permissions inferred from chat, production model activation.

## Further Notes

Owns the shared envelope baseline with other contract owners and integrates accepted P3 candidate configurations. Can build against versioned P1/P4/P5 doubles. Exit: native and MCP clients can operate one saved plan with equivalent authority, survive restart, and truthfully expose completion or limitation.

The parent issue defines shared contract ownership, parallel waves, integration acceptance and shared-file serialization. Test boundaries were confirmed by the user: shared authenticated application operations, with focused connector and AI-quality evaluation seams. Preserve existing safety, approval and release requirements; reconcile older conflicting priorities with the current artist-manager direction.

Related pipelines: [P1](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/6) · [P3](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/8) · [P4](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/9) · [P5](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/10) · [P6](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/11). Integration dependencies are described above; these links do not make all work wait for other pipelines to finish.

items.title: materialize-redshift: post-commit apply crash-loops on serializable isolation violation (1023) writing applied tokens
items.body:
## 1. Priority

High - a production materialization is fully stalled with no successful destination apply for 5+ hours and no clean workaround. Second tenant in 9 days. No data loss or corruption: the applied-token write is in the same transaction as the data, so a failed apply rolls back both. The impact is a hard stall and a growing backlog, not bad data.

## 2. Scope and prevalence

Theoretical blast radius: every `materialize-redshift` task running the post-commit-apply image (2026-08-29, #5110) whose Redshift metadata schema is shared with another materialization. #5110 shipped as a single unconditional code path with no feature flag, so every Redshift task is on it. Docs already advise at most one Redshift materialization per schema, but shared-schema setups exist in the field and worked before this change.

Observed prevalence: 2 tenants, 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-11.

- Tenant A, 2026-09-03: crash-looped on recovery, then recovered on its own ("limping along"). A sibling task on the same endpoint database and schema was identified at the time.
- Tenant B, 2026-09-11: fully stuck. 19 consecutive failures over 5h03m, zero successful applies. Customer-reported. Customer states all of their Redshift materializations are alerting.

Trend is worse, not better: the first occurrence self-recovered, the second does not.

## 3. Trigger (testable)

Two or more `materialize-redshift` tasks sharing the same endpoint `database` and `schema` (and therefore the same checkpoints table), committing concurrently, on the post-#5110 image.

The apply transaction now runs every binding's `COPY` / `MERGE` / `DELETE` first and only then takes the checkpoints-table lock, immediately before the token `UPDATE`. Where the apply takes minutes, the window in which a peer can commit against the same checkpoints table spans the whole apply.

Minimal repro input (synthetic, no customer data):

- Two `materialize-redshift` tasks, each one binding, configured with identical endpoint `database` and `schema` and distinct target tables.
- Enough rows per transaction that each apply takes tens of seconds or more (the failure needs an apply long enough for a peer to commit inside it; a sub-second apply will usually slip through).
- Run both concurrently against the same cluster. Expect `ERROR: 1023` on the token `UPDATE`.

Self-sustaining once triggered: the failure kills the connector, the shard restarts, and recovery re-drives the same pending entry through the same multi-minute apply, so each retry reopens the same window.

## 4. Root cause (if known) + confidence

Likely - the checkpoints-table lock moved from the first statement of the commit transaction to immediately before the token write, which does not serialize Redshift's snapshot-based isolation check.

`checkpointsTable.write` takes the lock as its first statement:

https://github.com/estuary/connectors/blob/main/materialize-redshift/state.go - `write()`, `lock %s;`

but `write` is itself the last thing `commit` does, after every binding's `COPY`, `MERGE` and `DELETE`:

https://github.com/estuary/connectors/blob/main/materialize-redshift/driver.go - `commit()`, `d.checkpointsTable.write(ctx, txn, tokensMap, legacyCheckpoint)` immediately before `txn.Commit`

#5110 records the intent: "It moves from the start of the transaction to immediately before the token write, shrinking the contention window from the whole apply to one small statement. All applies then take that single lock in the same order, so they cannot cycle." Same-order locking rules out lock-ordering deadlock, but Redshift evaluates serializable isolation over the transaction's whole read/write set against the snapshot taken at transaction start. A lock acquired after that snapshot does not prevent a conflict with a peer that committed in between. AWS guidance is to lock all tables at the beginning of the transaction, before performing any operations.

Not verified: the identity of the conflicting transaction. Confirming needs `stl_tr_conflict` / `sys_query_history` on the affected cluster, which support does not have access to.

Secondary lead, unverified: `ensureTokensColumn` runs `ALTER TABLE <checkpoints> ADD COLUMN checkpoint_tokens VARBYTE(1024000);` on every connector `Open` against the shared checkpoints table. Under a crash loop that is DDL on a contended table on every restart. Raised during the 2026-09-03 triage and neither confirmed nor ruled out.

Also relevant: 1023 is retryable and #5110 notes the token makes a retry safe, but listed retry-on-serialization-failure as out of scope. There is no retry path - `commit` returns the error, the connector exits 1, the shard fails.

## 5. Investigation steps / reproduction (testable)

Read the task's shard logs for the stall window (tenant B, 2026-09-11, 06:24Z - 16:18Z, single shard `00000000`).

Healthy through 23 consecutive rounds, apply durations 35s to 12m47s. Last successful apply:

```
2026-09-11T10:58:59Z  finished committing documents for resource  round=0 took=1.891476816s
```

First failure, in the normal transaction path:

```
2026-09-11T11:14:09.504530072Z  commit failed: writing applied tokens: ERROR: 1023 (SQLSTATE XX000)
2026-09-11T11:14:10.127681606Z  shard failed  error="runTransactions: app.ConsumeMessage: commit failed: writing applied tokens: ERROR: 1023 (SQLSTATE XX000)"
```

Every subsequent failure is in the recovery path. Second occurrence:

```
2026-09-11T11:21:00.490963265Z  commit failed: writing applied tokens: ERROR: 1023 (SQLSTATE XX000)
2026-09-11T11:21:00.494178094Z  shard failed  error="completeRecovery: store.RestoreCheckpoint: commit failed: writing applied tokens: ERROR: 1023 (SQLSTATE XX000)"
```

Last occurrence in the captured window, still failing:

```
2026-09-11T16:17:34.617090950Z  commit failed: writing applied tokens: ERROR: 1023 (SQLSTATE XX000)
2026-09-11T16:17:34.620771176Z  shard failed  error="completeRecovery: store.RestoreCheckpoint: commit failed: writing applied tokens: ERROR: 1023 (SQLSTATE XX000)"
```

Counts and shape over the window:

- 19 `commit failed ... ERROR: 1023` and 19 `shard failed`, first `2026-09-11T11:14:09.504530072Z`, last `2026-09-11T16:17:34.617090950Z`, ongoing at the end of the captured logs.
- 21 `started materialization recovery commit`, 2 `finished materialization recovery commit` (both at startup with nothing pending, 187.929us and 395.282us).
- Each failing cycle re-drives the same pending entry as `round: -1` against one resource, taking 2m34s to 8m05s before failing on the token write. Whole transaction rolls back; no rows land, no token is written.
- Restart backoff grew from ~45s to ~13min, so roughly one doomed attempt per 15-20 minutes.

A republish during the stall did not clear it - a new build applied and failed identically ~5m47s later:

```
2026-09-11T16:11:46.874748417Z  applying updated task specification
2026-09-11T16:17:34.617090950Z  commit failed: writing applied tokens: ERROR: 1023 (SQLSTATE XX000)
```

Checked and found nothing:

- `estuary/connectors` issues and PRs for `1023` / serializable isolation / checkpoints lock since the 2026-08-29 change -> no existing issue, no fix in flight.
- Connector changelog and #5110 -> confirms the lock relocation was deliberate and that retry-on-serialization-failure was scoped out.

## 6. Definition of done

- Acceptance: two `materialize-redshift` tasks sharing one endpoint database and schema commit concurrently for a sustained run with no `ERROR: 1023`; a task that hits a serialization failure mid-apply recovers without operator intervention rather than crash-looping; `commit failed: writing applied tokens` absent from logs over a 24h window on the affected tasks.
- Regression test: the section 3 trigger, codified - two tasks on a shared metadata schema, applies long enough to overlap, asserted to complete without a serialization failure. Include the recovery path specifically, since 18 of the 19 observed failures were in `completeRecovery: store.RestoreCheckpoint` rather than the normal transaction path.
- Constraints / do not break: exactly-once delivery for delta-updates bindings (the token is the only thing preventing duplication there); no forced backfill or re-version for affected tasks; no new Redshift privilege, role, or ownership requirement; the crossover path for tasks still on the legacy checkpoint format.

## 7. References

- Slack thread: <#integrations permalink, to backfill>
- #5110 - materialize-redshift: convert to post-commit apply. Introduced the lock relocation and scoped out retry-on-serialization-failure.
- Connector changelog entry 2026-08-29.
- AWS: serializable isolation troubleshooting - https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/c_serial_isolation-serializable-isolation-troubleshooting.html
- First occurrence 2026-09-03 triaged in an internal incident channel; not previously filed.

items.title: File & Document Security: authenticated attachment ingress + tenant auto-activation end-to-end
items.body:
## Objective (Greg-approved)
Integrate real, server-received file attachments into **existing** authenticated tenant checks, not a parallel scanner/dashboard. No attachment ⇒ file rules not applicable; matching real attachment ⇒ enable applicable implemented file rules by default unless tenant explicitly set Off. Preserve tenant stage/rule action authority, all findings and fail-closed responses. Production approval gate was removed on Nov 5, but security, cost and CI controls remain.

## Existing implementation and gap
- `guardoath/attachment_probe.py` does bounded byte-only classification for CSV and explicit unsupported formats; `guardoath/csv_formula.py` detects risky CSV spreadsheet formulas in CSV text.
- `guardoath/tenant_record.py`, `guardoath/models.py`, `guardoath/app.py`, `guardoath/engine.py`, `guardoath/static/*` are **Director/shared reserved**; the probe is not connected to an authenticated binary ingestion API, record `auto` behavior, or the dashboard. **No PDF/DOCX/XLSX inspection is currently supported.**
- Reference: `docs/file-document-security-architecture.md` and `docs/director-agent-coordination.md`.

## Ownership and sequenced deliverables
1. **Director/shared-file owner: acknowledge paths and ownership in coordination file** before editing reserved API/tenant/dashboard files. Design bounded authenticated attachment representation, strict received-bytes vs claimed MIME/extension provenance, budget, format detection, per-tenant metering, existing input/output flow and safe AI gating.
2. Add backward-compatible explicit tenant `auto` vs `off` semantics, preserving stored explicit-Off tenant records and independent input/output actions; allow rule-level exceptions without silently mutating a tenant during requests.
3. Wire detected CSV attachment bytes through existing `csv_formula` and per-stage tenant action evaluation, return all findings and strongest applicable action. Unsupported/malformed/over-budget files must be reported `incomplete`/`unsupported` and never pass as scanned or get forwarded unchecked to the AI when required inspection fails.
4. Director: use existing dashboard controls/Example Picker for actual synthetic attached bytes and distinguish saved action, effective action and `not applicable — no attachment`; no second UI.
5. Atlas can add **non-overlapping** scanner/fixture acceptance tests and documentation, but must not edit reserved paths without acknowledgement.

## Required acceptance matrix
- Zero attachments, one recognized CSV with dangerous and benign cells, quoted mention of a file without bytes, renamed extension/MIME, multiple CSV, CSV + unsupported PDF/DOCX, malformed/encrypted/oversized/ambiguous bytes, CSV BOM and escaped formulas.
- Explicit tenant Off, new-tenant Auto, persisted legacy Off, per-rule Off, per-stage Block/Flag/Allow, two simultaneous findings and strongest action, tenants A/B isolated and authenticated; no unauthenticated upload; metering limits and no raw-content echo.
- Fail-closed on required unchecked attachment and no unsafe AI call; inspect request/output stages independently.
- Focused pytest/browser + **13/13 Tests and 3/3 CodeQL** at implementation SHA; report actual deployed SHA and 15 live verification outcomes after controlled deployment. Never claim unsupported parsers implemented.

**Restrictions:** No new AWS resources, paid services, CI bypass, weakened tests or unilateral changes to Director-reserved paths. Release approval gate removal does not eliminate these safeguards.

**Required delivery architecture for Glovo Basket MCP v1:** Claude is the **development/release-candidate orchestrator**, not an independent production deployer. MCTL MCP / Control Plane is the preferred **control and audit surface** for any supported release/deploy/rollback operation. **GitOps remains the source of truth**, and ArgoCD/Kubernetes are reconciled through the platform's authorized workflows, never by ad-hoc Claude production commands.

### Responsibilities and operational decision tree

1. **Claude owns P0 engineering:** feature/Draft PRs, schema and API/UI code, OAuth/MCP integration and real-client harness, CI, independent semantic review, remediation, version/SHA and provenance evidence, and preparation of a single compatible release candidate + **inert** GitOps/ingress/rollback proposal. Do not infer that a tool exists solely from its name; verify that it supports the *platform bootstrap mctl-api release* rather than only tenant services.

4. **Supported MCTL control path:** if a first-party MCTL MCP release/deploy operation actually supports the platform bootstrap and the **exact required approvals, holds, provenance and point-of-effect policy**, use it after the corresponding authorization. Track its workflow id, final status, GitOps revision, image digest, Argo Sync/Healthy, rollback evidence and OAuth real-MCP-client smoke.
5. **Control-plane gap:** if there is no such platform bootstrap operation, document a *small, specific integration slice* for invoking the existing **authorized** bootstrap GitOps release workflow through MCTL MCP, with explicit check at point of effect. Do not build a parallel deploy framework, use ad-hoc `kubectl`/`helm`/Argo writes, trigger a generic tenant-service deploy, or introduce alternate release tags. Coordinate with existing [mctl-gitops#2528](https://github.com/mctlhq/mctl-gitops/issues/2528) release hold enforcement work instead of duplicating it.
6. **Authorization boundary:** `mctl-api#934` release hold, `gitops#2528` point-of-effect hold, required canonical digest-bound DevLoop approvals, independent review and production DB/roles/Vault/DNS/allowlist/activation gates **remain binding**. Use only a release path that both supports this service and is currently authorized. Writing a plan or this issue text does not confer deployment authority.
7. **Keep delivery moving:** an unavailable platform release adapter, pending owner decision, or other production-only gate must **not** block independent Draft PRs, CI, local disposable E2E, OAuth client compatibility work, or inert GitOps artifacts. Record a concise exact blocker packet and continue permitted work.

### Acceptance evidence

- Document the chosen **actual MCTL MCP operation/workflow** for platform `mctl-api`, or the source-backed missing capability and linked narrow integration task.
- One source-pinned Glovo Basket MCP release candidate and GitOps plan; verified immutable image/source match and rollback/kill switch.
- Separate effect-level deployment/activation authorization evidence; never equate CI PASS to a release GO.
- Ultimately a **real OAuth MCP client** using `https://glovo.mctl.ai/mcp` to submit a synthetic basket, a direct authenticated human approval, and a final MCP status with negative tenant/owner/replay checks. No Temporal, Telegram or provider dispatch required for this first release.

**Instruction to Claude:** treat this as part of the existing autonomous delivery loop, not an invitation to pause for new routine approvals. Any work that needs genuinely unavailable permissions must stop at the actual gate while all other authorized work continues.

---

## Owner directive 2026-11-10 — standing GO for autonomous non-production delivery

**This is the latest owner's instruction and overrides older wording below that prevented Claude from writing code or opening Draft PRs pending a separate confirmation.** User explicitly wants **no routine confirmation prompts** and an agentic delivery loop. The owner grants a **standing, narrow GO for non-production code authoring and Draft PR preparation** for this one issue, within the normal identity/repository permissions. This is NOT a canonical DevLoop approval, a valid `aar_` authorization, a merge/release/deploy/hold-lift grant, nor a claim that owner-only platform approval checks are satisfied.

### What Claude must do NOW, without asking again

- Start the next autonomous iteration from checkpoint 1 (issue comment [6780971244](https://github.com/mctlhq/mctl-api/issues/1006#issuecomment-6780971244)). It already confirmed there is no live DevLoop for this issue and no current implementation agent; **do not re-do the same feasibility investigation or wait for another GO to author a Draft PR**.

- In parallel, prepare a read-only source-grounded hold/release inventory for `mctl-api#934` and `mctl-gitops#2528`, plus inert GitOps, ingress/OAuth and rollout plans. Do not hold back local implementation due to unrelated platform/Temporal security DAG.

Write concise checkpoint evidence to #1006. **Never end an iteration with “should I proceed?”, “do you confirm?”, or “can I open the Draft PR?”** The answer for this scoped non-production work is already YES.

### Real authorization boundary — do not attempt to bypass

A non-human policy actor may authorize only when the canonical delegation/enrollment and checkpoint are actually live and scoped.

This issue cannot itself lift those holds.
- **Human basket approval always requires the actual authenticated basket owner**. Claude must neither approve a basket on their behalf nor introduce an MCP `approve=true` tool, even for synthetic baskets.
- Preserve real OAuth identity, tenant and owner checks, test against 2 tenants / 2 users, frozen basket fingerprint, consent expiry/revocation, no real Glovo provider access/orders/payments; UNKNOWN safety state remains BLOCKED for the corresponding effect.

### Non-blocking exception handling — no owner-question loop

2. Switch immediately to another authorized independent subtask: implementation Draft PR, tests, OAuth client harness, inert GitOps, read-only grants analysis, observability, review remediation, docs.
3. When **all** remaining paths are genuinely blocked, produce one final, consolidated GO/NO-GO packet with exact effect scopes and wait for external authorization/event. Never invent authorization, auto-retry a refused approval, spam reminders, or claim prod DONE.
4. Only mark DONE when a real OAuth MCP client reaches `https://glovo.mctl.ai/mcp` and an authenticated human decides a frozen synthetic basket, with negative tenant/auth/replay proof.

**Measurable next output:** one or more actual open `mctl-api` Draft PRs implementing the minimal vertical slice, with head SHAs, tests and a concrete remaining release/activation blocker table. A further design-only checkpoint is not a substitute.

---

## Owner scope pivot — minimal first usable MCP

Parent: [mctl-gitops#2457](https://github.com/mctlhq/mctl-gitops/issues/2457). Target **real** Streamable HTTP MCP over OAuth at `https://glovo.mctl.ai/mcp`, explicit selected team tenant, narrow allowlist and **synthetic catalog/baskets only**, terminating in a genuine **human approval decision**, not execution of any order.

**This slice supersedes the previous M1 direct fake-dispatch critical path as the FIRST user-facing release.** Do not gate this slice on Temporal frontend authorizer/security DAG, mctl-agents control workflow #1044, bridge provider worker, mctl-telegram facade/runtime, provider dispatch/sweeper or full fake-order E2E #990. Those are separate, **deferred** for a later execution phase, not cancelled or marked implemented. No Telegram login, Telegram bot or Telegram package must be required. Reuse vetted code/contract concepts without importing Telegram runtime dependencies.

### Architecture target

A minimal independently deployable `mctl-api`-owned Go MCP binary/module (prefer a separate `cmd/glovo-basket-mcp` image if reusing the held mctl-api monolith release would unnecessarily couple delivery; compare the actual release/hold applicability before selecting packaging). One HTTP MCP service with real OAuth resource discovery and authenticated calls, canonical MCTL principal/tenant checking, read-only synthetic catalog, basket persistence and an approval-request endpoint. PostgreSQL is sufficient. Use the existing MCTL authorization and human approval primitive wherever source-supported; do **not** invent an MCP `approve` tool or impersonate an owner. If the canonical `aar_` requires a Temporal execution to create, source-verify that dependency and design the smallest compatible no-Temporal integration or report that exact blocker; don't silently create a parallel unsound approval engine.

### MCP tool contract v0

- `glovo_list_products` — bounded synthetic catalog, fixed deterministic product identifiers/prices.
- `glovo_create_basket` — owner- and tenant-scoped basket, idempotent create.
- `glovo_update_basket` — add/remove/update quantity; server recomputes totals, no client-supplied price.
- `glovo_get_basket` — owner-only current snapshot.
- `glovo_request_approval` — transactionally freeze immutable basket snapshot + fingerprint, create canonical human approval request; return opaque request ref and approval URL/action. No order/provider effect.
- `glovo_approval_status` — pending/approved/rejected/expired (no cross-owner existence leaks).

After approval, the immutable snapshot becomes **approved only**, with no `place_order`, dispatch, payment, callback, provider command or fake execution. An update after submission creates a new revision needing fresh approval; an old approval never authorizes a new version. Human approval happens through MCTL identity-bound UI/API, not as an MCP/agent tool with `approved=true`.

### OAuth / tenancy / isolation

- Real OAuth/OIDC: issuer, exact resource audience, scopes, expiration, JWKS/appropriate verification, PKCE/client metadata/discovery appropriate to clients; validate on each request.
- Server-derived principal, explicit team tenant selection, membership check and finite operator allowlist. No `labs`, personal scope or Telegram identity fallback.
- Per-principal quotas, payload limits, duplicate/replay protection, audit without secrets, CSRF/nonce protections on human decision path.
- Negative proofs: missing/wrong audience, other tenant, different owner in same team, revoked user, stale approval, immutable snapshot mutation, forged approval and replay all refuse without changing approved state.
- No real Glovo APIs, credentials, account linkage, shopping-cart writes, scraping, checkout or payment.

### Why this is lower risk

No Temporal, no trusted control worker, no queue/signal/outbox, no fake provider worker, no cross-namespace credentials, no migration/transfer of existing WorkItems ownership merely to support fake dispatch. Add only necessary basket/approval storage and grants; verify production database/release constraints before touching any shared role/schema. Production exposure and credentials still require actual security, OAuth, GitOps and release gates. **No workaround of mctl-api#934, mctl-gitops#2528 or a held release through alternate tagging or duplicate production process.** A separately packaged independent MCP image must have legitimate release provenance and authorization and must not imply held API changes are deployed.

### Deliverables

1. Source-backed design choice: a small MCP service from mctl-api (one binary) vs existing API mount, which avoids the Telegram and Temporal dependency with fewest trusted boundaries. Document exact reusable identity/approval APIs and the release hold effect.
2. Minimal schemas, unit/API contract tests, OAuth real MCP-client harness (not a mock of MCP protocol).
3. Distinct immutable image digest/SBOM/provenance, least-privilege deploy package, DNS/HTTPS, health, rate/egress limits, rollback + kill switch.
4. Separate dark production rollout and allowlisted activation decisions via real authorization/release gates; scoped P1/P2 evidence, do not infer permission from issue text.
5. End-to-end proof: real OAuth login, tool discovery, synthetic basket edits, real human-approved immutable snapshot, status transition, 2 tenants and 2 principals, no external provider effect.

### Prior work to reuse or defer

- Reuse, after inspecting sources: mctl-api#958/#959/#960/#961 and existing human `aar_` authorization contracts, OAuth and tenant identity.
- **Deferred, not dependencies of this first slice:** mctl-api#1004, mctl-agents#1044, mctl-api#990 fake-dispatch matrix, mctl-gitops#2568/#2570–#2575 Temporal security, previous mctl-telegram facade/provider work, 3-image build plan.
- Existing Draft AMEND PRs #2578/#2579 and #2563 are not invalidated; do **not** merge, approve or implement them as a prerequisite to the simple MCP. Reconcile which parts can safely be reused; leave any active independent reviews alone.
- Existing governance work [mctl-gitops#2580](https://github.com/mctlhq/mctl-gitops/issues/2580) is a parallel autonomy improvement, **not a blocking prerequisite to doing authorized engineering work**.

### State, next gate

**Planning/intake only.** No permission granted here for proposal approval, implementer dispatch, merge, release, production DB change, hold removal, DNS mutation or canary activation. First step: repo/source read-only feasibility comparison, exact deployment path and minimal implementation proposal; apply DevLoop independently to this narrowly scoped issue. Human owner approval for basket is always required and cannot be automated.

items.title: [FC-05][P0] Bind external authorization to the exact submission command
items.body:
## Triage record

- **Stable key:** FC-05
- **Owner role:** Creative and fulfillment; reviewer: Product and frontend. Named owner/reviewer remain kickoff decisions.
- **Priority:** P0 — Only authenticated current authority for these exact terms may submit an external order.

## Current evidence

Inspected live GitHub 2026-10-10 at main [4c78849754ed542ca77d3b5e1831f8773f9b54b4](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/commit/4c78849754ed542ca77d3b5e1831f8773f9b54b4). The complete tree contains only README.md, docs/architecture/OWNERSHIP.md and ACCEPTANCE.md; all three were read. No AGENTS.md, runtime, lockfile, tests, workflows, adapters or migrations exist. README explicitly says documentation baseline only. Existing #1 is WP08; merged documentation PR #2 verifies no implementation. Acceptance remains planned.

## Scope / non-goals

Validate submit command and consume application-owned OrderAuthorization. Application issues/revokes authorization and owns payments/customer lifecycle; connector never mints it.

## Acceptance IDs and expected outcome

- [ ] FC-05.1: Require trusted tenant/project/order and logical operation, idempotency key, immutable approved bundle ref/hash, provider/product/options/quantity, quote identity/terms/currency/maximum amount, validated shipping payload with destination ref/digest/method, and authenticated external authorization ref. Browser flags/correlation IDs confer no authority.
- [ ] FC-05.2: Server-authenticated verifier checks issuer/audience/service identity as applicable, ownership, expiry/revocation and exact quote/provider/product/quantity/destination/bundle binding immediately before dispatch. Missing/stale/forged/cross-tenant/replayed/mismatched auth or verifier outage fails closed with zero provider submit.
- [ ] FC-05.3: Replay with a new purchase identity is rejected. Safe same-command retry returns FC06 existing attempt/result without a second consume or dispatch. Persist binding atomically; require external claim/consume semantics where issuer contract requires it. Changed/expired terms need externally renewed authorization; artwork approval alone is insufficient.

Mapping: FC-05.1–3; FUL-02. Local cases supplement original global procedures.

## Approach and migration implications

Resolve issuer verification and atomic consume/replay protocol with application/shared-contracts before real calls; missing upstream contract blocks integration. Store minimal immutable auth refs/decision metadata/digests, not auth secrets. Recheck quote, preflight and external budget before FC06-controlled dispatch.

## Blocked-by / blocks / related links

- Parent: [FC-EPIC](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/1).
- Blocked by local prerequisites: [FC-01](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/3), [FC-04](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/9), [FC-08](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/10), [FC-06](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/11), [FC-10](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/6), [FC-11](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/5)
- Upstream accepted contracts/artifacts: [shared-contracts/issues/26](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/26), [getticketstub.com #16 — purchase-authorization issuer and customer handoff](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/16)
- Blocks: [FC-02-SANDBOX](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/15), [FC-12](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/16).
- Fixtures can unblock development; closure needs scoped accepted upstream artifacts, not unrelated epic completion.

## Executable validation

Run one valid case plus separate missing/stale/revoked/issuer/tenant/order/provider/product/quantity/destination/shipping/currency/amount/bundle mismatches and verifier outage. Every rejection asserts zero submit calls. Race copies and retry consumed command: one order/existing result; reuse auth with new identity fails.

```sh
./scripts/verify-fulfillment --suite authorization --mode simulated --evidence-dir evidence/FC-05
```

## Required evidence for closure

FUL-02 authorization record and invalidation cases, verifier contract review, sanitized rejection matrix/counters and integrated replay trace.

Closure requires reviewed implementation links, exact component SHAs and contract/runtime versions, actual commands and exit results, sanitized fixtures/assertions, relevant trace/attempt/artifact references, and explicit environment plus billing_mode (simulated/sandbox/live). Keep full addresses, contact details, secrets, auth tokens, signed asset URLs and raw provider errors out of public evidence. Missing evidence stays pending. The command below is a future implementation requirement: no runner exists or was executed during triage.

Shared schema ownership stays in [shared-contracts](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/blob/main/docs/contract-catalog.md); preserve the [master acceptance IDs, procedures, priorities and evidence](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/integration-evals/blob/main/planning/acceptance-checklist.json). FC-* IDs are local additions. No payment capture, checkout, authorization issuance, creative generation, financial ledger or final profitability belongs here. No provider call or charge is authorized by this triage.

## Cross-repository audit correction — 2026-10-10

- [ ] FC-05.4: Race two distinct submission identities/idempotency keys against one still-valid single-use authorization. Across concurrent workers and restart, prove at most one issuer-authorized claim and at most one provider order/dispatch for the authorized logical purchase. Losers return conflict/existing-intent evidence; they cannot mint a new authority or fall back to a new key. Same-command re-observation must not consume again.
- [ ] FC-05.5: Revoke or expire authorization, quote or external budget reservation after queuing but before transport; also change bundle/spec/destination/amount. Each invalid case yields zero new provider submits. Missing verifier/claim outcome fails closed or remains unresolved under #11; it cannot be treated as an unconsumed authorization available for another purchase.

**Explicit blocker/decision owner:** this issue coordinates the authenticated claim/consume/replay protocol with issuer [getticketstub.com #16](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/16) and canonical [shared-contracts #26](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/26). These links establish the owner, not an accepted atomicity guarantee. Record the actual issuer endpoint/implementation SHA, canonical schema/version, claim identity/lifetime, restart behavior and jointly reviewed negative/concurrency fixtures before integrated closure. Consume the issuer/verifier deliverable before full GT-07 customer-journey closure: GT-07 itself consumes connector submission/status/sandbox evidence, so requiring both whole issues to close first would create a cycle. Artwork approval is separately owned by [getticketstub.com #15](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/issues/15) and is not purchase authorization. Budget authority remains [cost-intelligence #12](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/cost-intelligence/issues/12) using [shared-contracts #12](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/12).

Run these cases in the existing authorization suite and attach sanitized issuer claim history, connector attempt IDs, per-identity dispatch counts and real issuer/consumer conformance results. Synthetic credentials/recipients are fixtures; a local fake issuer alone cannot close integration.

items.title: [Phase 3.1] Connector and tool schema

milestone.title: Phase 3
milestone.description: Connector & Tool Layer — Composio (re-evaluation in ADR-0003), tool execution runtime, tool-proposal API for agent self-modification at the tool layer, common connectors. Tracker: #26.

items.body:
## Parent

- Master goal: #4
- Phase tracker: #26

## Phase goal

Migrations 013..N for the connector / tool / proposal schema, plus the small migration generalizing Phase 2's `proposal_triggers` with a `target_kind` discriminator. RLS on every tenant-scoped table. Versioning triggers for `tool_manifests` / `tool_manifest_versions`. DTOs only — no business logic in this PR.

## Problem statement

Phase 3 cannot land any service code until the schema exists. This is a focused, low-risk infra PR so reviewers can scrutinize the data model in isolation before behavior layers on top.

## Non-goals

- Composio SDK wiring (3.2)
- Policy engine logic (3.3)
- Execution runtime (3.4)
- Proposal endpoint (3.5)
- Connector implementations (3.6)
- Any business logic. Controllers, services, and most NestJS providers are out of scope; only the schema migrations, DTOs, and the `proposal_triggers` generalization.

## Hard prerequisites (block-on)

- [ ] ADR-0003 `Status: Accepted` (defines table shapes, encryption-at-rest column type, `proposal_triggers` generalization choice §Q6, idempotency-key scope §Q9)

## Approved architecture / ADR link

`docs/adr/ADR-0003-connector-and-tool-layer.md` — §Q2 (OAuth storage), §Q3 (encryption), §Q6 (proposal_triggers), §Q9 (idempotency key), §Q12 (connector account isolation), §Q17 (migration runner).

## Tasks and subtasks

- [ ] `backend/db/migrations/013_connectors.sql` — `connectors` (definition: id, slug, name, version, auth_mode, capabilities JSONB, manifest_schema JSONB) — global table, NOT tenant-scoped (definitions are shared)
- [ ] `backend/db/migrations/014_connector_accounts.sql` — `connector_accounts` (per-tenant per-user; encrypted credential blob per §Q2/§Q3; lifecycle state: pending|authorized|revoked|expired) — RLS-scoped
- [ ] `backend/db/migrations/015_connector_sessions.sql` — `connector_sessions` (active session state, refresh timing) — RLS-scoped
- [ ] `backend/db/migrations/016_tool_manifests.sql` + `tool_manifest_versions.sql` — canonical manifest definition + immutable versioning trigger per the `004_config_tables.sql` pattern; columns: `proposal_source` (`'human_edit'|'agent_reflection'|'tool_failure'|'import'`), `proposal_context` JSONB, `parent_version_id` self-FK
- [ ] `backend/db/migrations/017_tool_invocations.sql` — `tool_invocations` (FK to `step_runs.id` from Phase 2.1; idempotency_key per §Q9; status, started_at, finished_at, error_class, cost_usd, cost_tokens, result_cache_key) — RLS-scoped
- [ ] `backend/db/migrations/018_tool_policies.sql` — `tool_policies` (per-tenant per-tool: allow/deny, approval required, rate limit bucket key, redaction policy ref, dry_run_required) — RLS-scoped
- [ ] `backend/db/migrations/019_proposal_triggers_target_kind.sql` — generalize Phase 2.5's `proposal_triggers`: add `target_kind` enum (`'workflow_version'|'tool_manifest_version'`), default existing rows to `'workflow_version'`, add CHECK constraint
- [ ] Paired down migration for each
- [ ] DTOs in `backend/src/connectors/dto/`, `backend/src/tools/dto/` — input/output schemas only, no service classes yet
- [ ] Unit tests for each migration's up/down round-trip via the integration harness

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pnpm migrate:up && pnpm migrate:down && pnpm migrate:up` round-trips cleanly
- [ ] RLS verified: a query made under `SET app.tenant_id = 'A'` cannot see rows owned by tenant B for `connector_accounts`, `connector_sessions`, `tool_invocations`, `tool_policies`
- [ ] `tool_manifests` versioning trigger fires: inserting a new version increments `version_no` and preserves the prior row immutably (mirroring `workflow_versions`)
- [ ] `proposal_triggers.target_kind` exists, defaults `'workflow_version'`, and accepts `'tool_manifest_version'`
- [ ] Encrypted credential column round-trips a fixture token using the chosen encryption mechanism (per ADR-0003 §Q3)
- [ ] DTO contract tests pass
- [ ] No business logic in this PR — `git diff --stat` should show migrations + DTOs + tests only

## QA and validation plan

Required:
- [ ] `pnpm test` — DTO validators
- [ ] `pnpm test:integration` — migration up/down + RLS isolation + versioning trigger
- [ ] `pnpm migrate:up && pnpm migrate:down` against a clean Postgres
- [ ] Verify column-level encryption with a fixture: insert plaintext via SQL with encryption call → SELECT returns plaintext only when the right key is set

Manual QA:
- [ ] `psql` walkthrough of each new table; confirm constraints, indexes, RLS policies match the ADR

## Rollback plan

- Every migration has a paired down step
- Feature flag `CONNECTOR_TOOL_LAYER_ENABLED` (default `false`) — even with tables present, no surface is exposed without it
- Encryption key rotation is documented in the ADR; key compromise scenario triggers `scripts/revoke-all-connector-accounts.sh` (runbook)

## Reuse pointers

- `backend/db/migrations/004_config_tables.sql` — immutable versioning trigger pattern (copy for `tool_manifests`)
- `backend/db/migrations/003_rls_policies.sql` — RLS template
- `backend/db/migrations/012_proposal_triggers.sql` (from Phase 2.5, #45) — table being generalized here
- `backend/src/workflows/dto/` (from Phase 2.4, #44) — DTO style to mirror

## Self-modification surface

This issue lands the *schema* for Class C tool-manifest drafts. The endpoint that writes those drafts lives in 3.5 (#54). The `proposal_triggers.target_kind` discriminator means tool-failure-triggered proposals flow through the same drain queue as workflow proposals.

## Architecture confirmation required

- [ ] ADR-0003 `Status: Accepted` before merge

## Links

- Tracker: #26
- Master goal: #4
- ADR-0003: #49

items.title: Phase 1W2: provision truly isolated CXOps staging within budget — owner gate
items.body:
# Phase 1W2 — Staging provisioning decision and acceptance contract

## Goal
Allow the owner to log into **real isolated CXOps AI staging** and safely create synthetic test tenants, tickets, handoffs and staff replies. No live customer data, production credentials, real Zendesk calls, production notifications or real AI spending.

**Engineering prerequisite:** Draft PR #36 — https://github.com/zrasooli94/cxops-ai/pull/36 (preview login/public/backend routes fail closed, including a built-server smoke test with a zero-call loopback backend).

**Other development:** PR #35 remains the tested interactive *fictional* demo; PR #33 remains a separate held security migration. Do not merge/deploy either as a side effect.

## Budget preflight — do not spend or provision yet
Official plan references (October 2026):
- Render: https://render.com/pricing — free web service at $0 subject to limits, small paid web instance about $7/month; per-service usage/bandwidth may add expense.
- Neon: https://neon.com/blog/neon-free-plan-1-gb-per-project — Free plan offers up to 100 projects, with per-project storage and compute caps. **Create a new empty project, never branch from production**.
- Nhost: https://nhost.io/pricing — Starter $0 but only **one active project per Starter organization at a time**; Pro starts around $25/month. Do not infer user's account entitlement or create a second active tenant automatically.
- CXOps operating budget target is **under $50/month total**, counting existing production infrastructure. Actual existing account plans/charges and Nhost tenant options have not been verified.

Two candidate topologies:
A. **Prefer no incremental fixed cost** when accounts allow it: Render free dedicated staging service + independent Neon Free project + separate active Nhost Starter tenant (if eligible). Confirm that 512MB Render free service is sufficient and can stay available for testing.
B. **Fallback requiring explicit owner budget approval:** Render 0.5 CPU/512MB staging service ~$7/mo + isolated database on eligible free allowance + independent Nhost tenant; Nhost Pro may add ~$25/mo depending on organization requirements. Existing production costs must be included before authorization.

## Safety requirements (hard gates)
- [ ] Written budget/owner approval for *any potentially billable* staging infrastructure; no automatic upgrading.
- [ ] Confirmed new **empty** Neon staging project, unrelated to production branch snapshots, DB credentials not shared.
- [ ] Verified disposable synthetic schema/fixtures, database network credentials scoped to staging only.
- [ ] Separate Nhost auth project and test users; independent JWT issuer, audience and membership; no production account password reuse.
- [ ] Render staging service based on explicit branch SHA, manual deployment, no prod env vars; notifications, AI spend, real Zendesk webhooks/writebacks and worker external side effects disabled.
- [ ] Vercel Preview variables branch-scoped; `BACKEND_API_URL` differs from production and points only to staging; flags set **last** after independent isolation audit.
- [ ] Browser smoke: login, logout, tenant selection, A/B tenant separation, handoff assign/release/resolve and clean rollback using synthetic data.
- [ ] Verify zero traffic to production by source + audit logs.
- [ ] Independent review and final owner approval before any public-facing staging exposure.

## Stop conditions
Existing Nhost Starter org only permits one active tenant; staging backend cannot run within free tier; lack of empty Neon DB; source is production clone; any uncertain cost; backend with prod secrets; insufficient tenant isolation.

## Status
**PLANNED, NOT PROVISIONED.** The CI preview blocker is verified separately; this issue is the handoff to a complete authenticated staging system, not permission to create infrastructure or change production.
