items.title: Complete AI Docs serving and portable inference/MCP acceptance
items.body:
## Purpose

Preserve the remaining AI acceptance work during repository consolidation:

- [Original AI issue 225: public Docs serving qualification](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ai-platform/issues/225)
- [Original AI issue 231: portable consumer inference and MCP](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ai-platform/issues/231)
- [Consolidation corrections in PR 1](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/pull/1)

This issue tracks completion of those two existing requirements. It does not close the original issues or claim a new hosted release. A source commit or passing CI alone does not establish the serving and interoperability acceptance below.

## Existing implementation

The Docs source already contains static-host assistant availability gating, canonical version handling and the Docs package's own validation dependency resolution. Qualify those existing fixes instead of implementing a duplicate or enabling an assistant gateway merely to fill a navigation link. The public-site symptoms recorded in issue 225 were observations from 28 October; current serving behavior must be checked afresh.

The AI source already has the bounded `onesa-inference-v1` text client, Onesa and OpenAI-compatible adapters, a stateless endpoint and an optional local MCP stdio bridge. PR 1 adds early model/credential validation and retains backend/request provenance in the client and its Drone copy. Those bounded corrections are not full provider compatibility or external MCP qualification.

## A. Public Docs serving acceptance

- [ ] Qualify the exact public Docs source and artifact through its existing independent release process. Run the clean locked Docs-only validation, actual browser/accessibility checks, classified assets, search, PDF and provenance checks.
- [ ] On the actual public site, static-host navigation leads to useful working actions; capability descriptions distinguish implemented source from currently available synthetic scope; hero, footer and generated outputs share the canonical documentation version.
- [ ] Verify readable search previews, useful guide ranking and exact API operation deep links.
- [ ] Reconcile Company and Robot capability wording with their independently accepted scope without implying that a Company or Docs publication releases a new Robot component.
- [ ] After any authorized publication, verify the canonical serving artifact and anonymous denial of internal content. Preserve failed results. Keep public and protected Docs as separate release decisions.

Public source references: [Docs configuration](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-frontend/apps/docs/docusaurus.config.ts), [public homepage](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-frontend/apps/docs/src/pages/public-home.tsx), [Docs acceptance runner](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/scripts/docs/acceptance.mjs), [classified-output validation](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/scripts/docs/validate.py), [search regression tests](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/scripts/docs/test_search_content.py).

## B. Portable inference and MCP acceptance

- [ ] Complete the versioned consumer contract for capability discovery, messages, generation, bounded streaming, cancellation, usage and redacted failures. Reject unavailable, unauthorized or unsupported capabilities before transmitting consumer data; document the exact supported API profile and limits.
- [ ] Demonstrate the same consumer integration scenario through Onesa and at least one alternative adapter with unchanged application business logic, tool integration and stored domain records. Keep provider-specific sessions, identifiers and response formats inside adapters.
- [ ] Document and verify portable message/history records and export behavior. Preserve existing records across provider changes; retain actual provider/model/revision and known usage for each generation without silently truncating context or relabelling old output.
- [ ] Keep chat inference and embeddings/indexes separately identified. An embedding change requires explicit compatibility, reindex and rollback acceptance.
- [ ] Establish explicitly scoped authenticated consumer identity, approved server-side credentials/endpoints and tenant isolation. Test cross-user denial, revocation, cancellation, malformed responses and injection; discovery or a model response must not grant authority.
- [ ] Complete the required versioned MCP tools/context integration, including resources/prompts and discovery/authorization beyond the present local two-tool bridge, and qualify an authenticated external client against the declared protocol profile.
- [ ] Demonstrate explicit failure/fallback behavior: no silent cross-provider transmission and no deterministic output represented as live inference. Preserve independent Robot and Drone safety authority; model or MCP output cannot authorize physical operation.
- [ ] Complete the separately approved, bounded live-provider and authenticated MCP-client acceptance. Local synthetic fixtures do not establish hosted operation or authorize new provider processing, credentials, paid inference or model downloads.

Public source references: [full interoperability requirement](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/docs/product/PRD.md#interoperable-ai-integration-requirement--2026-10-28), [consumer client](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-backend/app/consumer.py), [stateless endpoint](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-backend/app/consumer_api.py), [local MCP bridge](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-backend/app/mcp_stdio.py), [consumer regressions](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-backend/tests/test_consumer.py), [Drone integration profile](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-drone/integrations/onesa-ai/README.md).

## Completion record

Record a sanitized outcome for each checklist item, identifying the reviewed public source and applicable public check results. Keep secrets, private source bundles and operational receipts out of this public issue. Both acceptance tracks must be satisfied before closing this consolidated tracker.


### Observed 5 November 2026

The public site was checked anonymously against its currently served provenance, legacy revision `d8a0807f43dfd83388927cdb1e84bf058ed81286` (documentation `0.3.0`). Eleven independent browser/HTTP checks passed: matching hero/footer/PDF versions, useful static-host actions, readable search previews, authentication-guide ranking, an exact API-operation deep link, five internal-content denials, eleven classified public PDFs, and the homepage at 320/1440 pixels in light/dark mode with no accessibility violations in those four observations.

The full current-source acceptance **failed** because the served applications menu still labels the Robot link “Onesa AI Robot”, while the pinned current registry says “Onesa Robot”. These observations do not establish a canonical-source deployment, full-site acceptance, independent Company/Robot releases, or retirement eligibility. The failed result is retained.

[PR DruHustle/onesa-ug#13](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/pull/13) adds scoped MCP resources/prompts and request cancellation. Its exact-head CI and all 31 post-merge dev checks passed. The official [MCP Python SDK 2.3.0](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/releases/tag/v2.3.0), in a separate client process, passed 14 interoperability checks against the unchanged adapter, an actual TLS API and disposable PostgreSQL with real migrations. Both low-level and high-level clients negotiated protocol `2025-11-25`. Checks covered scoped discovery, an actual arithmetic tool call, owned resources, cross-account denials, untrusted prompt text, document deletion, session revocation and default-deny scopes. TLS certificate/hostname verification stayed enabled; all fixtures were removed. The model resource correctly reported mock inference, and no model generation was requested.

This proves local external-SDK interoperability. A dedicated deployed service identity, hosted external-client acceptance, live-provider inference contracts and the rest of both original acceptance tracks remain open; this issue is not complete.

Local requirement namespace: **SC-01**; preserve existing global **CON-01, CON-02, CON-03** where applicable, without renumbering or treating structural validation as end-to-end verification. [Master definitions and evidence](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/integration-evals/blob/main/planning/acceptance-checklist.md) remain authoritative.
- [ ] SC-01.1: For every contract record schema path/version, source-of-truth owner, producer, consumers, trust boundary, lifecycle, semantic authority, field steward and leaf issue; no missing contract is hidden in this inventory issue.
- [ ] SC-01.2: Reconcile ArtifactHandoffManifest (creative artwork to print-production) versus ProductionBundle (print output to app/fulfillment); ApprovalReference/Receipt versus OrderAuthorization (art approval versus purchase).

- [ ] SC-01.4: Maintain requirement -> owner issue -> dependencies -> executable verification -> closure-evidence map, including every SC-01 through SC-12 requirement; no invented consumer or global ID.

## Approach and migration implications
Use SC-02 canonical JSON Schema and generated ESM/TypeScript bindings with pure validators. Inspect existing downstream local shapes and fixtures at immutable revisions, record differences, and agree adapters with one producer and one consumer before removing any local type. Never silently rename semantics or claim a local prototype is canonical. Pin schema version, shared-contracts source SHA/package version and consumer revisions together; preserve old-version tests per SC-03.

**Parent:** #1 (WP01 / SC-EPIC).
**Blocked by:** [SC-02](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/5) — canonical schema and toolchain agreement is required for machine-validatable inventory entries and executable validation; inventory inspection can proceed in parallel.

items.title: security: replace unconditional runtime RLS policies with tenant/store isolation
items.body:
## Production blocker
Migration `db/migrations/0033_security_prodx_app_role.sql` grants DML on all public tables and creates a policy for every table with `USING (true) WITH CHECK (true)` for `prodx_app`. This makes RLS effectively non-restrictive for the runtime role and does not enforce organization/store boundaries. `0034_security_enable_rls_all_tables.sql` then enables RLS across the public tables.

This is confirmed by inspecting the migration and applying the current migration set to an isolated PostgreSQL 17 test instance. Do not apply migration 0033 to production as written.

## Required engineering work
- Inventory every public table and classify it as tenant/store scoped, global reference data, or internal migration/operations data.
- Trace authenticated principal organization/store context through HTTP routes, services, repositories, connection pool, and transaction boundaries.
- Design transaction-local, connection-safe tenant context for database RLS (no session state leaking between pooled requests; no client-supplied tenant identity).
- Add RLS policies with least privilege using the verified server-established context. Internal/global tables must receive explicit policies or privileges justified by schema-level evidence.
- Remove broad DML grants where not required; preserve required financial/inventory atomicity, idempotency, and audit behavior.
- Add PostgreSQL integration tests proving cross-store and cross-organization SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE are denied, allowed same-store operations work, and pooled connections cannot leak tenant context across requests.
- Verify migrations upgrade/downgrade and policy catalog; do not weaken or skip security gates.
- Update migration 0033 before deployment or add a deterministic follow-up migration that safely removes its broad policies; ensure fresh-install and upgrade paths converge without duplicate migration heads.

## Acceptance criteria
1. No `prodx_app` policy has unconditional `USING (true)` or `WITH CHECK (true)` on tenant-scoped data.
2. Runtime role remains `NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS`; it cannot read or mutate another tenant/store's rows even when application SQL omits a store predicate.
3. Tenant context is derived from authenticated server principal, set transaction-locally, and cleared automatically on commit/rollback/release.
4. PostgreSQL integration tests demonstrate isolation and pooled-connection reuse.
5. Full required CI, database/security/architecture gates pass.
6. No production migration/deploy until these conditions and live runtime verification pass.

## Related
- PR #265: https://github.com/Prodx-organization/PRODX-POS/pull/265
- Current production `/api/v1/healthz`: HTTP 200
- Current production `/api/v1/readyz`: HTTP 503 (request ID `3c0511b5-c9f8-42bf-9582-f1ab29714b43`)
- Current status remains **NOT PRODUCTION READY**.

items.title: [Spec] P1 — Intake and reusable library
items.body:
# P1 — Intake and reusable library

Parent specification and coordination: https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/5

Status: ready for manager decomposition after assignment. No implementation, paid experiments or rollout dispatched by this issue.

## Problem Statement

Artists cannot conveniently reuse work if uploads lose context, recovery requires repeated transfers, or imported and new assets behave differently. Partial recovery can also be mistaken for a complete backup.

## Solution

Make artist-controlled imports and direct uploads converge on a private, reusable catalogue with stable asset identity, preserved source contexts, visible readiness and retry-safe recovery.

## User Stories

1. As an artist, I want to upload new work once and reuse it, so that subsequent releases do not require another transfer.
2. As an artist, I want to resume interrupted intake, so that completed work is preserved.
3. As an artist, I want to retry a lost upload confirmation safely, so that I receive the same usable asset.
4. As an artist, I want to recognize filenames and source labels after reload, so that I can find the right work.
5. As an artist, I want to import selected or recent posts before the entire archive, so that I can prepare a release immediately.
6. As an artist, I want to retain distinct source publications for shared media, so that captions and publication history are not lost.
7. As an artist, I want to keep previews and originals distinct, so that a similar image is not mistaken for an interchangeable asset.
8. As an artist, I want to see unavailable or partial media clearly, so that I know which work needs repair.
9. As an artist, I want to export retained files with their available context, so that I can recover them independently.
10. As an artist, I want to retain convenient Patreon intake through credential changes, so that security improvements do not create a manual reupload chain.

## Implementation Decisions

- Own asset readiness, source/version association, durable intake metadata and recovery. Reuse existing MediaAsset, canonical shared-media history, gallery SHA suppression and export services; their existence does not mean intake-wide replay and association are complete.
- Preserve direct presigned private tenant-scoped object storage. Revalidate commits against stored bytes and ownership. A repeated successful commit should return its saved result without silently accepting a different payload.
- Preserve source snapshots separately from Relay-owned presentation and reuse state. Exact-byte reuse must not expose another creator's assets or erase distinct source contexts; similarity is not authority to merge variants.
- Publish the reusable-asset contract with identity, source revision, readiness, retained rendition/original status, labels, audience classification and permitted retrieval. Consumer references must remain stable across retries.
- Make useful selected work available while broader history continues. Preserve current Patreon repair, reconciliation and live access guards; do not change release evidence or restart its queue.
- Inventory current branch behavior before slicing filename, batching, recovery, limits and staging issues; active workspace changes may already address some earlier findings.
- Before changing credential custody, document parity for existing imports, new posts, restricted media, browser closed/offline behavior, retries and user actions. If parity fails, harden the current approach rather than force migration.

## Testing Decisions

- Primary seam: authenticated intake and Library reads with isolated database state and a controlled object-store adapter.
- Prove lost-response replay, reload/restart recovery, missing bytes, mismatched commit data, expired presigns, wrong creator, preserved source contexts and distinct variants.
- Prove imported work enters preparation without public Relay publication or download/reupload, and private intake leaves patron permission behavior unchanged.
- Prior art: upload route/storage tests, private staging access, canonical shared-media integration, SHA duplicate suppression and Patreon media-repair tests.

## Out of Scope

New fan entitlement services, new external sources without a scoped demand/capability case, replacing the storage architecture, global cross-tenant deduplication, publication approval, full backup claims without restoration proof.

## Further Notes

Can start inventory, failure fixtures and upload/recovery slices independently. Supplies asset/provenance contract to P2/P4/P5/P6. Integrates after the shared contract gate; preserves the current Patreon acceptance gates. Exit: one uploaded and one imported item remain privately usable with context across retry/restart and prepare a release without retransferring bytes.

The parent issue defines shared contract ownership, parallel waves, integration acceptance and shared-file serialization. Test boundaries were confirmed by the user: shared authenticated application operations, with focused connector and AI-quality evaluation seams. Preserve existing safety, approval and release requirements; reconcile older conflicting priorities with the current artist-manager direction.

Related pipelines: [P2](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/7) · [P3](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/8) · [P4](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/9) · [P5](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/10) · [P6](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/11). Integration dependencies are described above; these links do not make all work wait for other pipelines to finish.

items.title: Epic: bootstrap FDE Agent Platform outcome-delivery control plane
items.body:
## Objective
Build the public, domain-neutral FDE Agent Platform as an **Outcome Delivery OS** that converts enterprise intent, evidence, expert behavior, policies, systems, and baselines into governed Digital Employees; executes only through constrained, durable, observable controls; and binds technical receipts to measurable outcomes without collapsing Human authority or private/public boundaries.

## Shared procedural authority

Every unfinished issue is directed by canonical procedures from:

```text
ed3c/skills-shared@ec5a240fa3cbafda2c6a8bce0ae12143e0992f80
```

Canonical binding and no-vendoring policy: #14.

Skill bodies, shared system prompts, reference procedures, scripts, schemas, and architecture rubrics remain in `skills-shared`. `fde-agent-platform` stores only repository-specific bindings, profiles, task packets, product code/adapters, synthetic fixtures, tests, and exact-subject receipts. No local `SKILL.md` or mirrored canonical `skills/` body is allowed.

## Foundation stack

1. #2 / PR #5 — repository control plane and Shadow Architecture governance.
2. #3 / PR #6 — public contracts and synthetic fixtures.
3. #4 / PR #7 — deterministic Role Pack + Tenant Overlay compiler.
4. #14 / PR #24 — exact external `skills-shared` binding and executable no-vendoring controls.
5. #47 / PR #48 — Agent read order, directory State Machines, full Issue DAG, data flow, and molecular Git Town Stack-PR index.
6. #13 — exact Git Town, local Forgejo, worktree, reconciliation, Actions, and publication receipts.

The executable documentation entrypoints are the root `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture/README.md`, `docs/governance/issue-dag.md`, and `docs/governance/stack-index.md` on PR #48. They index consumer-specific state and requirements; canonical Skill bodies remain external.

## Business, engagement, and organizational plane

- #25 — opportunity triage, baseline, Outcome Charter, and Bounded Value Pilot.
- #42 — full FDE engagement lifecycle and phase-gate orchestration.
- #18 — Human FDE Workbench, process-owner review, approvals, and executive governance.
- #37 — Internal FDE enablement, Domain Champion training, adoption, and handoff.
- #20 — managed operations, SLOs, incident ownership, FDE capacity, and termination.
- #36 — hybrid managed-service pricing, outcome settlement candidates, and SLA credits.

## Evidence, data, and context plane

- #26 — multi-source engagement evidence ingestion, redaction, and entity disambiguation.
- #45 — Data-for-Agent semantic contracts, quality, lineage, and schema/meaning drift.
- #8 — bitemporal Evidence Graph and Current-State Process Twin.
- #27 — provenance-aware retrieval and minimal sufficient ContextPack assembly.
- #29 — PostgreSQL persistence, bitemporal tenancy, migrations, and append-only audit.
- #33 — private Tenant Overlay resolver and exact-digest handoff across dual forge.

## Design, authority, and compilation plane

- #15 — Role Pack, Tenant Overlay reference, Outcome Contract, and compiled-spec registries.
- #28 — WorkflowSpec / ChangeSpec DSL, compiler, and target-state workflow architect.
- #9 — Policy Gateway and Connector Capability Registry.
- #22 — tenant isolation, secrets, MCP/tool authorization, and threat-model evals.
- #44 — enterprise SSO, directory roles, approval signatures, delegation, and access lifecycle.

## Integration, execution, release, and observability plane

- #30 — typed Connector SDK, synthetic capability adapters, and MCP gateway boundary.
- #10 — deterministic durable-runtime simulator, Runtime Receipts, and drift reconciliation.
- #40 — real durable-orchestration adapter, persistent timers, outbox, and crash recovery.
- #17 — simulation, risk-weighted progressive authority, Change Controller, and rollback.
- #32 — trace correlation, audit integrity, redaction, and outcome linkage.
- #34 — SaaS-rich, platform-centric, legacy, private-VPC, and air-gapped deployment profiles.
- #46 — first authorized private read-only/draft System-of-Record connector canary.

## Evaluation, model, learning, and evidence plane

- #31 — multi-layer Eval Pack registry, replay harness, mutation controls, and architecture receipts.
- #12 — model registry, routing policy, version pinning, shadow dual-run, and release train.
- #16 — expert-behavior trace store and governed candidate-Skill mining.
- #19 — failure clustering, reusable asset extraction, and portfolio productization.
- #35 — governed repair routing and post-training dataset lifecycle.
- #23 — independent validation of Varick/Lingyang claims and benchmark artifacts.

## Outcome and economics plane

- #11 — Outcome Ledger, attribution, unit economics, dispute, and settlement-ready records.
- #25 — pre-engagement baseline and counterfactual contract.
- #36 — value-aligned commercial model without automatic invoicing.

## Product and developer surfaces

- #38 — bounded customer-support, sales, marketing, operations, and finance Role Pack catalog.
- #39 — typed API, SDK, CLI, plugin contracts, and synthetic integration examples.
- #21 — first complete synthetic AP invoice/PO exception Digital Employee capstone.

## Assurance and production-readiness plane

- #41 — load, chaos, backup/restore, disaster recovery, capacity, and Human-review budgets.
- #43 — enterprise assurance-control mapping and evidence-pack generation without self-certification.
- #46 — exact private sandbox connector admission before any real deployment claim.

## Hard invariants

- Customer evidence, identities, credentials, private policies, system mappings, private Tenant Overlays, and customer-specific connectors never enter public GitHub.
- Tenant Overlays may restrict a Role Pack but never widen authority.
- Prohibited actions survive composition, release, model changes, retry, recovery, and handoff.
- Generated artifacts bind exact normalized input digests, contract versions, environment, and evidence subjects.
- Parsed documents, retrieval results, model output, expert behavior, external case reports, and business telemetry are candidates/evidence classes, not self-authorizing truth.
- Deterministic policy owns authorization, transition legality, accounting, idempotency, reconciliation, and release-blocking invariants.
- Natural-language requests become typed ChangeSpec candidates; they never execute directly.
- Git Town, Forgejo, local verification, GitHub Actions, publication, merge, release, production, commercial settlement, and business outcomes remain separate evidence lanes.
- Shared procedures direct execution but cannot grant merge, publication, permission, credential, legal, financial, release, or production authority.
- Source-reported external cases never count as this repository's runtime or outcome PASS.
- Planned directories, branches, PR atoms, providers, and state transitions remain explicitly `PLANNED` or `NOT_EXERCISED`; documentation cannot promote them.

## Evidence boundary

Current GitHub connector work can observe/create GitHub issues, branches, commits, and draft PRs. Live local Forgejo, Git Town executable, linked worktrees, private Tenant Overlay resolution, exact-head Actions, real identity/connector/model providers, production runtime, customer acceptance, commercial settlement, and business outcomes remain `ABSENT`, `NOT_EXERCISED`, or `HUMAN_ADMIT_REQUIRED` until their owning runtime/organization emits exact-subject evidence.

## Completion rule

This epic closes only when every linked issue is either:

1. completed at its explicitly declared evidence ceiling with exact-subject receipts; or
2. terminated, superseded, or redirected with a reasoned disposition and affected dependency routes updated.

A mentioned Skill, source-reported case, green leaf branch, successful model response, sandbox canary, documentation diagram, or transport-level success cannot close the epic by itself.

items.title: [Audit][Roadmap] Ragbot platform architecture audit and prioritized execution plan
items.body:
## Executive summary

Audit baseline: `main` at the September 2026 architecture after durable worker reliability, staged knowledge generations, parser/chunker ports, Golden Dataset and parser/PDF benchmark work.

Ragbot is already beyond a prototype RAG application. Its strongest current properties are:

- PostgreSQL-backed durable ingestion queue with lease/heartbeat/retry/DLQ/reconciliation
- staged source knowledge generations with PostgreSQL activation authority and durable Qdrant cleanup
- dense Qdrant + PostgreSQL CJK-aware lexical hybrid retrieval + RRF + reranking
- Parser/Chunker ports and promotion benchmarks
- multi-tenant ACL/RBAC enforcement
- SaaS/local/object-source ingestion coverage
- Prometheus/OpenTelemetry plus quality benchmark infrastructure
- OpenAI-shaped compatibility API and a preliminary Node client

The next architecture risk is **integration growth without stable platform contracts**. Current factories and ingestion dispatch still branch on implementation/source names; model routing is not wired as the production composition boundary; embeddings are synchronous; vector index schema has no first-class lifecycle; persistence has a legacy inheritance stack/fat repository; and the SDK/identity/object-storage surfaces are not yet at the same maturity as the ingestion core.

The recommendation is therefore **not** to add dozens of providers/connectors/vector databases immediately. First establish stable extension and index contracts, then expand implementations behind them.

---

## Priority 0 — platform correctness and evolvability

### #50 Platform registry / typed runtime profiles
Make connector/model/embedding/vector/upload implementations resolvable behind one stable registry and shared config/capability schemas.

### #51 LLM provider/router plane
Wire capability-aware model routing into production; remove global environment mutation; add OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Azure/Bedrock/Ollama adapters behind one contract.

### #52 Embedding plane
Replace synchronous embedding transport with bounded async batching/retry/rate-limit handling and a complete embedding contract identity.

### #53 Vector index lifecycle
Introduce versioned indexes, shadow validation, Qdrant alias activation and rollback for embedding/vector-schema upgrades.

### P0 exit criteria

- adding a provider/connector no longer requires editing core dispatch switches
- model and embedding clients use pooled bounded transports with explicit capabilities
- every indexed chunk can be associated with an immutable embedding/index contract
- incompatible embedding changes build a new index and support atomic cutover/rollback
- current production paths remain regression-compatible

Do not start broad provider/connector expansion before these boundaries are stable.

---

## Priority 1 — production platform surface

### #54 Connector SDK
Standardize snapshot/incremental/checkpoint/deletion/ACL/rate-limit semantics and then validate with SharePoint/OneDrive, Azure/GCS, Slack/Teams or other new connectors.

### #55 Storage architecture
Split the monolithic `Repo`, retire the `postgres_repo -> pg_repo -> managed_pg_repo` inheritance stack and clarify transaction/capability boundaries.

### #56 PostgreSQL performance gates
Keyset pagination, SQL-side filtering, COPY/staging batch paths, queue claim/reconciliation hot-path cleanup, pool/timeouts and query-plan benchmarks.

### #57 Retrieval engine
Move hybrid retrieval to a reusable async/composable pipeline. Keep current hybrid RRF as control, then benchmark Qdrant dense+sparse, alternate fusion, MMR and multi-vector plans.

### #58 Public API / SDK / MCP
Freeze versioned knowledge/search contracts, add maintained Python+Node SDKs, typed retry/error/pagination/stream semantics and a scoped MCP/tool surface.

### #59 Upload object storage
Keep `UploadStore`, add S3/MinIO first and then Azure Blob/GCS, including direct upload and lifecycle/GC semantics.

### #60 Enterprise identity/security
Add OIDC/JWT, service accounts, hashed/rotatable API keys and unified SecretResolver backends while preserving Ragbot RBAC/ACL as authorization truth.

### #61 Durable quality/observability
Tie production requests and evaluation runs to parser/chunker/embedding/index/retrieval/reranker/model contract IDs; use benchmark evidence as promotion gates.

### P1 exit criteria

- platform can horizontally scale API/workers without shared upload PVC
- source catalog/job APIs remain bounded at large cardinality
- retrieval has deadline/cancellation and measurable stage-level latency
- Python and Node consumers have supported, versioned SDKs
- operators can identify exactly which data/model/index contracts produced a response
- identity/secrets no longer depend on one static plaintext API-key mapping pattern

---

## Priority 2 — controlled capability expansion

### #62 Multimodal RAG
Preserve tables/images/layout and visual citations in the normalized document/index contracts, benchmarked against the text-only baseline.

### #63 Release governance
Remove roadmap drift, lock/constraint CI/runtime dependencies, add SBOM/security/compatibility checks and mechanically validate capability/version documentation.

P2 can be partially parallelized, but multimodal indexing should wait for #52/#53 and object artifacts should build on #59.

---

## Dependency graph / recommended order

1. **Foundation:** #50
2. In parallel after the foundation shape is agreed: **#51, #52, #55**
3. Build **#53** on the embedding/index contract from #52
4. Run database operational work **#56** alongside storage consolidation, but do not delay obvious pagination/hot-path regressions
5. Use the registry in **#54 and #59** rather than adding new branches
6. Refactor retrieval in **#57** after the embedding/index interfaces are stable; preserve the current RRF path as the benchmark control
7. Productize **#58** over stable public contracts rather than exposing internal service objects
8. Implement **#61** across all preceding work so promotion decisions become evidence-based
9. Harden enterprise identity with **#60** before positioning Ragbot as a multi-tenant shared service
10. Add **#62** multimodal representations only after index/artifact lifecycle is explicit
11. **#63** begins immediately and stays cross-cutting

---

## Architectural principles to freeze

1. PostgreSQL is the authoritative control-plane/system-of-record store; Qdrant is a derived vector index.
2. Source publication and vector-index publication are different lifecycles; both require atomic activation/rollback semantics.
3. Product semantics/config schemas live in stable handwritten contracts; vendor adapters sit behind them.
4. Connectors emit normalized source changes; parsers emit normalized document blocks; chunkers emit chunks; embedding/index stages do not reach back into vendor connectors.
5. Tenant/ACL filtering happens before evidence is returned, not as a post-generation cleanup.
6. New retrieval/vector techniques are promoted by Golden Dataset + latency/cost evidence, not by feature novelty.
7. Public API/SDK contracts are smaller and more stable than internal service classes.
8. Production network clients use pooled transports, bounded concurrency, explicit deadlines, retries and structured errors.
9. Secrets and identity are references/claims, not arbitrary plaintext configuration fields.
10. Runtime capabilities and release documentation should be machine-verifiable.

---

## Industry baseline used for the audit

- LangChain: common provider/document-loader/vector-store interfaces and separately packaged integrations
- Haystack: composable pipeline components + distinct Document Store abstractions
- Unstructured: source/destination connector architecture, optional connector packages and configurable ingestion stages
- Qdrant: dense+sparse/named vectors, multi-stage Query API and atomic collection aliases for vector-version cutover
- Weaviate / Azure AI Search: explicit hybrid fusion + reranking stages and multi-tenant/filter-aware retrieval
- Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases: decoupled Retrieve vs RetrieveAndGenerate, metadata filtering, reranking, structured/multimodal knowledge paths and retrieval traces
- Vercel AI SDK: provider registries/capability normalization
- OpenAI / Anthropic SDKs: typed streaming/errors, configurable timeout/retry and provider transport concerns kept out of application logic

This audit intentionally treats these products as architectural references, not dependencies to copy wholesale.

---

## Overall target state

Ragbot should converge from a feature-rich RAG service into a **versioned Knowledge Retrieval Platform** with five explicit planes:

1. **Connector/Ingestion plane** — durable source sync, parsing/chunking, generation publication
2. **Index plane** — embedding contracts, vector/sparse indexes, version/cutover/rollback
3. **Retrieval plane** — filters, candidate retrieval, fusion, rerank, evidence/citations
4. **Model/Agent plane** — provider registry, capability routing, bounded tool/model execution
5. **Control/Developer plane** — PostgreSQL metadata/jobs/evals, identity/RBAC, observability, SDK/MCP/admin

The existing code already contains many of these concepts; the next milestone is to make the boundaries explicit enough that new integrations can grow without destabilizing the core.

items.title: [Spec] Relay artist manager — coordinated delivery and parallel manager pipelines
items.body:
# Relay artist manager — coordinated specification

Status: reviewable specification. Implementation and manager dispatch are separate actions. Current product direction governs this program; existing delivery restrictions remain binding.

## Problem Statement

Working visual artists have artwork and publication context spread across platform accounts and local files. They repeatedly find assets, reconstruct captions, choose public previews, prepare releases and check whether publication succeeded. Existing Relay components address parts of that work, but the artist cannot yet rely on a consistent manager that remembers goals, prepares a useful plan, follows it through and learns from results. Generic AI advice does not remove that operational burden, and historical backlog directives can send development toward unrelated fan-network or monetization work.

## Solution

Offer a bounded artist-manager cycle: receive existing and new work, understand the artist's goal and constraints, prepare concrete releases, obtain the appropriate approval, manage supported execution and return with evidence-based advice. Preserve convenient Patreon imports and current access protection. Make new uploads reusable without requiring publication to Relay. Allow direct controls and conversation to operate on the same saved plan.

Develop six manager-owned pipelines in parallel around shared application contracts: intake/library; runtime/MCP; AI evaluation and tuning; release execution; evidence/outcomes; artist experience and business validation. One integration lead coordinates shared boundaries and acceptance without creating a second implementation team or new runtime system.

## User Stories

1. As an artist, I want to receive work from accounts I control, so that I do not have to download and upload my archive manually.
2. As an artist, I want direct upload for new work, so that I can prepare releases before publishing elsewhere.
3. As an artist, I want useful pieces available before a complete archive finishes, so that I can begin work immediately.
4. As an artist, I want interrupted intake to recover visibly, so that I know what remains and avoid repeating completed work.
5. As an artist, I want source captions, dates and links retained where available, so that imported art keeps its context.
6. As an artist, I want originals and previews associated without being conflated, so that I can select the right version.
7. As an artist, I want repeated intake associated safely, so that retries do not create confusing duplicate work.
8. As an artist, I want retained assets available for export, so that I can recover my work independently of future publishing.
9. As an artist, I want incomplete recovery identified, so that I do not mistake partial imports for a verified backup.
10. As an artist, I want to state my business goal and current capacity, so that Relay proposes a sustainable plan.
11. As an artist, I want explicit preferences distinguished from Relay's guesses, so that a suggestion does not become an unwanted rule.
12. As an artist, I want existing and new artwork considered together, so that useful older work remains available.
13. As an artist, I want Relay to explain candidate choices, so that I can judge their fit.
14. As an artist, I want a concrete short-term release plan, so that I do not have to translate generic advice into tasks.
15. As an artist, I want exact destination accounts, media, copy and timing visible before approval, so that I understand the proposed actions.
16. As an artist, I want to revise plans in chat or direct controls, so that I can use whichever is faster.
17. As an artist, I want unresolved restrictions or missing assets called out, so that Relay does not silently substitute unsafe content.
18. As an artist, I want approval for preparation distinguished from publishing authority, so that reviewing a plan does not unexpectedly publish it.
19. As an artist, I want changes to approved payloads handled explicitly, so that my original approval cannot authorize different content.
20. As an artist, I want truthful connector capability information, so that I know which releases require my presence.
21. As an artist, I want a ready handoff when manual publishing is required, so that I do not rebuild the submission.
22. As an artist, I want successful publications recorded separately from attempts, so that my release history is trustworthy.
23. As an artist, I want partial failures repaired without repeating successful destinations, so that retries do not duplicate posts.
24. As an artist, I want pause and cancellation honored, so that Relay respects changes in my plans.
25. As an artist, I want saved work to survive closing the browser, so that I can resume without repeating decisions.
26. As an artist, I want to use a supported external assistant with the same records and permissions, so that changing interfaces does not fork my plan.
27. As an artist, I want timely briefings on work and outcomes, so that I do not have to initiate every management session.
28. As an artist, I want missing analytics distinguished from zero results, so that I do not draw false conclusions.
29. As an artist, I want advice tied to my chosen goal, so that engagement is not substituted for commission or membership outcomes.
30. As an artist, I want uncertain attribution labeled, so that estimated results are not presented as proven sales.
31. As an artist, I want the next recommendation to account for previous results and feedback, so that Relay improves the ongoing workflow.
32. As an artist, I want my account access enforced regardless of the assistant used, so that another user or malicious imported text cannot act on my work.
33. As an operator, I want model changes evaluated before promotion, so that a cheaper or newer model does not silently reduce quality.
34. As an operator, I want costs and repeated artist use measured, so that we can determine whether the service is viable.
35. As a manager agent, I want explicit ownership and dependencies, so that parallel work does not create duplicate planners or overwrite shared contracts.
36. As a reviewer, I want each delivery claim tied to tested behavior and environment, so that local fixtures are not mistaken for production readiness.

## Implementation Decisions

- Preserve existing Account, Tenant and creator ownership. Do not activate multi-studio ownership as a side effect.
- Preserve normalized tier truth and the separation of source access, patron entitlement and presentation overrides. Private artist reuse does not weaken existing fan-facing access enforcement.
- Keep presigned direct object-storage uploads, private tenant-scoped keys and existing MediaAsset identity. Extend existing deduplication, source/version provenance and export behavior where gaps exist.
- Reuse the existing planning, revision, approval, distribution and schedule services. The runtime manager must inventory overlapping model/provider paths and select ownership explicitly; no assumption that every model call already uses one facade.
- Store the artist brief and plan state independently of a chat transcript. Preserve provenance for inferred preferences and explicit acceptance of consequential changes.
- A model proposes bounded structured actions. Application services validate ownership, asset references, capabilities, restrictions, freshness, budgets and authority.
- Native UI and MCP call the same authenticated application operations. An MCP tool invocation or model-generated approval field cannot substitute for authenticated approval evidence.
- Maintain distinct preparation approval, exact payload confirmation and actual publication evidence. Keep creator-finished publishing for the currently supported extension lanes.
- Connector capability is explicit per account and media/action type. Adding unattended image delivery or standing delegation is a later scoped amendment with connector evidence and revocation tests.
- Execution uses saved payloads and durable retry/reconciliation behavior. Uncertain external success must not trigger blind resubmission.
- Analytics services compute facts; model output interprets them. Metrics retain source, window semantics, freshness, missingness and attribution class.
- AI evaluation/tuning is an independent development pipeline using versioned fixtures, real adapters and controlled budgets. Fine-tuning model weights is out of scope initially.
- Reconcile changes to persisted state, plan semantics and approval scope through a shared contract review before implementation. Managers propose necessary additive schema changes; this specification does not preselect a new set of tables or wire field names.
- Scope the first integrated release to existing supported image workflows and verified accounts. Broader source, format and destination coverage requires a capability proposal, not an implicit promise.
- No fan-network, Tip economy, full website migration or live-trend-provider expansion belongs to this program.

## Testing Decisions

- Primary acceptance seam: authenticated application operations for intake, plan preparation/revision, approval, execution and outcome reads. Assert observable saved state and external effects, not private helper call order.
- Reuse real-service/database API scenarios for plan revision, restart, replay, tenant isolation and concurrency. Use isolated test tenants and controlled provider adapters.
- Add thin native UI/MCP conformance checks around that shared seam; neither adapter may bypass authority checks.
- Exercise connector boundaries with deterministic success, failure, timeout and ambiguous-success simulations. Real-account acceptance is a separate explicitly authorized release check.
- Evaluate model judgment against versioned development and held-out cases. Keep statistical quality evaluation distinct from deterministic security and execution tests.
- Use existing upload, staging, gallery provenance, conversational-planning, Goal Cycle, Rhythms, permission-parity, attribution and reminder test families as prior art.
- Acceptance includes restricted originals, unavailable evidence, late catalogue matches, expired credentials, revocation after approval, stale revisions, duplicate delivery attempts, cross-tenant IDs, timezone changes and interrupted sessions.
- A green model evaluation does not waive application invariants. A green mocked integration does not establish real-platform reliability.
- Record pre-existing failures and environment limitations without silently broadening implementation to fix unrelated work.

## Out of Scope

Custom foundation models or weight fine-tuning; a multi-agent marketing department; generic agent infrastructure; guaranteed growth or historical analytics completeness; new social networks chosen without demand; automatic publishing through unsupported connectors; new billing prices or usage allowances; fan discovery, Tips, Boosts and marketplace expansion; full membership-site construction; multi-studio activation; unrelated refactors; production rollout or paid evaluation execution authorized merely by this spec.

## Further Notes

The primary hypothesis is repeat paid value from managing releases using the artist's body of work. Validate completed releases, decision/correction burden, recurring use, catalogue reuse and operating cost. Archive recovery that only earns one-time use may warrant a separate service; this spec does not automatically pivot the business.

Managers may decompose their pipeline into vertical slices after assignment. They must first reconcile current working-tree evidence and existing contracts. The specification is not a claim that all described capability already exists, and reading it does not authorize automatic implementation dispatch.


### Parallel manager program

Status: specification and manager handoff package. No implementation, paid evaluation, external posting or deployment is dispatched by this package.

### Read order

Read the current product direction, the coordinated specification, this coordination guide, then the assigned pipeline specification and current implementation evidence. Older queues and model assignments are historical unless explicitly retained for the new assignment. Preserve existing permission, approval, safety and deployment requirements. Existing uncommitted work requires ownership reconciliation before editing.

### Manager assignments

| Pipeline | Manager owns | First independent deliverable | Integration dependency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 Intake/library | Asset readiness, source/version association, upload/recovery and context | Baseline inventory, replay/recovery scenarios, reusable-asset contract | Existing identity/access/storage authorities |
| P2 Runtime/MCP | Brief persistence, manager run orchestration, shared authenticated operations, MCP adapter | Authority map and context/result envelope | P1 asset, P4 capability/approval and P5 evidence contracts |
| P3 AI quality | Corpus/oracle, prompts/context/model experiments and promotion evidence | Offline scenario matrix and development/heldout protocol | Versioned envelope; later real P2 adapters |
| P4 Execution | Capability, exact-payload approval, schedule/handoff/reconciliation and receipts | Capability inventory and connector failure fixtures | P1 assets and P2 operation identity |
| P5 Evidence | Facts, coverage, outcomes, workflow-value telemetry and pilot protocol | Evidence semantics, synthetic fixtures and baseline measurement protocol | P1 provenance, P2 goals, P4 receipts, P6 interaction events |
| P6 Experience | Brief/plan/review/resume/attention/outcome journey and direct controls | Journey states and fixture-driven acceptance | Shared operations plus P1/P4/P5 projections |

One integration lead maintains shared contract versions, conflict resolution and release evidence. This is a coordination role, not a seventh product subsystem.

### Contract ownership

| Contract | Owner | Required reviewers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reusable asset and source/version readiness | P1 | P2, P4, P5 |
| Brief, context/result envelope, plan/revision identity | P2 | P3, P6 |
| Capability, action approval, execution and publication evidence | P4 | P2, P5, P6 |
| Metric/evidence/outcome envelope | P5 | P2, P3, P6 |
| Evaluation protocol and candidate package | P3 | P2 and integration lead |
| Review/interaction/effort events | P6 | P2, P5 |

The initial contract gate freezes semantics and representative fixtures, not a speculative replacement schema. Resolve existing authorities for each concept. Changes require a versioned proposal and affected consumer review. Additive compatibility is preferred; incompatible changes include a migration/replay plan.

### Parallel development waves

#### Wave 0: baseline and shared contract agreement

Each manager inventories current behavior and uncommitted work in its area, identifies existing tests and authority, and returns a bounded slice proposal. P2 coordinates the envelope, with P1/P4/P5 owning their records. P3 and P6 produce scenario and journey fixtures in parallel. No team waits for the full archive, live analytics or a new connector to start this work.

Exit: ownership is explicit, fixtures describe the same identities/status/approval meanings, and baseline limitations are recorded. No runtime or paid-run claim follows from this gate.

#### Wave 1: independent development

P1 closes upload/recovery and association gaps. P2 implements bounded orchestration over existing services. P3 develops/evaluates candidates against frozen fixtures and real adapters when available. P4 develops capability and reconciliation behavior with connector doubles. P5 implements facts/outcome semantics and instrumentation contracts. P6 builds review/resume states against those contracts.

P3's paid experiments may run in the background only under a separately recorded budget and stop policy. Fixture/scorer work can proceed without live keys. Candidate promotion never happens automatically.

#### Wave 2: integrated supported journey

Integrate an imported item and a direct-uploaded item through private readiness, concrete proposal, manual revision, preparation approval, exact action confirmation, supported delivery/handoff, publication evidence and outcome review.

Use existing image/destination capabilities. Unsupported formats and broader connectors stay visibly unavailable; do not enlarge scope to make a demonstration appear universal.

#### Wave 3: release evidence and business validation

Run isolated integration and applicable installed-extension/actual-account acceptance under the existing release rules. Record environment and pre-existing failures. Obtain the normal rollout authorization before activating runtime or MCP exposure.

Use the predeclared workflow comparison and pilot protocol to evaluate repeat usefulness, artist effort, archive reuse, willingness to pay and cost. Preparing the protocol does not authorize recruitment, messages, billing or a paid pilot.

### Integration acceptance

1. One owned imported asset and one uploaded asset survive retry/restart with source context and no additional transfer for reuse.
2. Native and MCP operations apply identical authorization and revision rules to the same saved plan.
3. Plan and exact action approval are distinct; a stale or modified payload cannot borrow earlier approval.
4. Manual connector steps are visible before approval. Composer opening is never reported as publication.
5. Partial failure and ambiguous success reconcile without duplicating already completed releases.
6. Missing metrics remain unknown; evidence-backed interpretation and hypotheses are distinguishable.
7. The artist can resume and revise through direct controls or conversation without conflicting plan state.
8. Candidate AI quality evidence is reproducible, contains failures/costs and has an explicit rollback target.
9. Existing Patreon access/ownership safeguards continue to pass applicable regressions.
10. All readiness claims distinguish fixture, isolated service, installed browser, actual account and production evidence.

### Shared-file and dispatch discipline

Managers own their pipeline's domain changes, not unrestricted access to every consumer. Schema/migrations, server registration, shared API clients, job registration, application shell/navigation and extension protocol are serialized integration surfaces. The lead assigns one writer and a scoped change window; other managers submit contract changes rather than editing those surfaces concurrently. Independent work can continue against fixtures.

No destructive git actions, wholesale schema replacement or cleanup of another team's changes. New assignments reconcile applicable nested agent instructions and retained legacy constraints; this program does not silently reassign live work.

Each manager handoff records: baseline; acceptance scenarios; owned changes; shared-contract requests; blockers; tests/evidence; environment limits; rollback; and the next bounded slice. “Ready for agent” means ready for a manager to decompose after assignment, not already released or automatically authorized to execute.

### Decisions retained for later scopes

- Exact model/provider and numeric quality/cost budgets: proposed by P3 before paid measurement, reviewed before activation.
- Broader source/destination/media coverage and unattended delivery: capability-specific amendment with P1/P4 evidence.
- Billing prices/allowances and paid pilot: separate business decision.
- Website/membership migration, fan network and custom model training: remain outside this program.


### Pipeline issues

- [ ] [P1 — Intake and reusable library](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/6)
- [ ] [P2 — Managed runtime and MCP](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/7)
- [ ] [P3 — AI quality, evaluation and tuning](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/8)
- [ ] [P4 — Release execution and connectors](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/9)
- [ ] [P5 — Evidence, outcomes and business validation](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/10)
- [ ] [P6 — Artist manager experience and plan integration](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/11)

Test boundaries confirmed by the user: shared authenticated application operations, with focused connector and AI-quality evaluations. These are manager-level specifications, not a queue of automatically dispatched implementation tickets.

items.title: 🔧 [chore] plan shared multi-environment module workflow
items.body:
## Problem
Module development must work consistently through ChatGPT + Remote Desktop Commander, Codex Cloud, and ChatGPT + GitHub, including five independent module chats. Current instructions and runtime assumptions are local-first; GitHub CI also has a clean-checkout build-order failure.

## Owner requirements recorded 2026-11-10
- Before every module build, give the owner a plain-English overview of 10–15 sentences explaining the result, scope and approach; wait for approval.
- Owner chooses the execution environment for that module.
- Use Super Build for every module; retain the installed skills and honest capability reporting.
- Plan each module so another chat/agent can resume from GitHub without hidden conversation history.
- Support five concurrent chats on independent modules, with GitHub tracking throughout.
- Every completed module produces a PR; owner reviews and explicitly instructs merge.

## Proposed setup (awaiting overview approval)
1. Put the mandatory approval/dispatch rules in the shared root AGENTS.md and reconcile conflicting instructions in AI_CODING_INSTRUCTIONS.md and CLAUDE.md without deleting business rules.
2. Extend the existing GitHub issue contract with overview, approved plan revision, chosen environment, assigned chat/session identifier, branch, base SHA, dependencies, allowed files, shared-contract/migration ownership, acceptance criteria, verification commands and handoff evidence.
3. Before implementation, record which chat owns each approved module. Five chats may run independent branches/worktrees and disposable databases; shared files/contracts or dependency chains are sequenced by the coordinator. An assignee alone is insufficient when all chats use the same account; use distinct session identifiers. Do not claim comments provide an atomic distributed lock.
4. Use one coordinator for dispatch and integration; module chats operate only on their assigned issue and never drain the whole Ready queue or run crash-recovery sweeps over other active chats. Every merge remains owner-directed and serial.
5. Adapt the installed Super Build lane to the selected issue and environment, preserving upstream tooling. A GitHub connector cannot execute a shell runner: it must hand off to a verified authorized execution environment, or explicitly report blocked. Do not call a manual source edit an executed headless Super Build run.
6. Prepare repository-owned setup and verification instructions for Codex Cloud and GitHub CI, resolve clean-checkout declaration build order in a separate coherent change, and prove runtime/package-manager choices rather than copying machine-specific paths.
7. Configure the actual Codex Cloud environment using the owner's connected account, repository, isolated development database and required network access. Repository files alone do not constitute an activated cloud environment. If account setup is unavailable, record the exact remaining activation step.
8. Keep requirements in canonical docs and workflow records in GitHub issues/PRs. Avoid competing permanent module specifications; approved issue plans reference the canonical SRS.

## Approval and safety boundaries
This issue is a planning record, not permission to start product modules. Existing test restrictions remain until the owner explicitly changes them. Planning/overview approval permits only the named module and chosen environment; it never grants merge, production deployment, production-data use or destructive migrations. Material plan changes require a revised overview and fresh scope approval. Never execute work from a stale chat without reconciling GitHub state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Owner approves the 10–15 sentence setup overview before implementation.
- [ ] Shared instructions unambiguously require overview approval, selected environment, scoped Super Build, GitHub records and review-before-merge.
- [ ] Each module has a reproducible execution contract and a distinct owner session, branch/worktree and isolated database.
- [ ] Five module plans demonstrate independent scopes or explicit serialization of shared contracts/migrations; no chat can silently claim another module.
- [ ] Remote, cloud and GitHub execution capabilities are checked separately and reported honestly, including the GitHub-only runner limitation.
- [ ] Codex Cloud activation and setup verification have actual evidence, or a named account/access blocker.
- [ ] Draft PRs contain actual command results, source SHA, remaining blockers and handoff steps; nothing auto-merges.

## Risk
Medium: cross-chat coordination and execution readiness. Approval and source ownership must remain explicit; instruction-only rules cannot guarantee perfect agent behavior.

## Blocked by
- None.

Status: owner approved the 13-sentence overview on 2026-11-10; scoped implementation authorized.


## Approved BUILD lane execution contract
- Owner approval: current conversation, message "Approved", following the 13-sentence overview recorded in this issue. Method: ChatGPT orchestrator + Remote Desktop Commander for repository preparation.
- Assigned session: root/workflow_setup; coordinator root owns Codex Cloud UI activation and separate CI workflow repair.
- This BUILD lane implements shared instructions, issue contract, and minimal repository-owned cloud setup/verification instructions/scripts only. No actual account activation or CI edits in this lane.
- Allowed files: AGENTS.md, AI_CODING_INSTRUCTIONS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/agents/issue-tracker.md, existing canonical docs/CURRENT_STATE.md, docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/AI_HANDOFF.md, docs/NEXT_TASKS.md, SRS_AND_BUILD_GUIDE.md; minimal scripts under scripts/dev/ and optional existing .codex configuration pointers. No new business specification documents.
- Read AI_CODING_INSTRUCTIONS.md in full before implementation. Preserve domain/UI rules. Latest owner-approved setup reconciles always-start-local-server requirements for read-only/connector-only modes: runtime startup remains required when actually verifying an interactive module; report unavailable runtime honestly instead of pretending startup.
- Cloud setup uses repository Node20 manifest/pnpm9.15.9 without changing runtime versions, global installations, database migrations or secrets. The recorded local Node24 compatibility probe is not cloud readiness proof.
- Explicitly retain current no-test-suite/no-new-test policy. Owner-approved operational setup/check scripts are infrastructure tools, not test suites. Shell syntax and real static gates may run; do not run pnpm test.
- Keep implementation under400 changed lines. If it grows, keep a coherent scoped draft PR and record remaining scope on this issue. No merge, close, production action or unrelated cleanup.

items.title: P1: Build trusted device enrollment, key revocation and authenticated lease control plane
items.body:
## Objective
Turn the policy and durable reservation foundations into a real trust boundary. The current policy crate validates signed approvals but does not itself enroll devices, own a trusted registry, expose authenticated endpoints or execute workloads.

## Required work
- Implement an authoritative device enrollment registry with lifecycle states, tenant binding and auditable ownership.
- Store trusted device/admin public keys in a protected registry; implement rotation and revocation with monotonic versions.
- Authenticate every lease acquire/renew/release request and bind it to device, workload, manifest digest, tenant and expiry.
- Add replay protection and clock-skew policy at the authenticated service boundary.
- Protect durable ledger integrity with a keyed MAC or signature whose key is outside the writable ledger directory; design recovery/rotation.
- Add restart, tampering, stale key, revoked device, replay, clock-skew, cross-tenant and concurrent reservation tests.
- Keep execution dispatch and sandboxing out of scope until control-plane authorization is independently verified.

## Acceptance criteria
- Caller-supplied keys cannot establish trust.
- A writer who can modify ledger files cannot recompute valid integrity without the protected key.
- Revoked/un-enrolled devices cannot acquire or renew leases.
- All authorization failures are fail-closed and auditable.
- Threat model and API contract reviewed before any remote execution integration.

items.title: [Research][Node Architect] Connector result-set completeness receipts for pagination-safe negative evidence
items.body:
## S1 paired research record

**Jira:** https://nhatnguyenquang1838.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-631  
**Pair state:** `PAIR_SYNCING`  
**Repository:** `nhatnguyenquang1838-coder/gwc`  
**Research snapshot:** `main@668a8645a696e4cbf84124201a58d26bc833f0c1`  
**Execution mode:** `chat_connector_only`  
**Boundary:** research-only; no code, implementation branch/PR, merge, deploy, release, production/config/data/secret/migration/destructive action.

## Research Question
How should Node Architect prove that a connector/search result set is exhaustive enough before treating absence, non-match, or dedupe-negative as evidence when APIs return pages, cursors, server-side caps, partial fields, permission-scoped views, or mutable collections—so `no match in the retrieved page` never silently becomes `no match exists`?

## DEDUPE
`DEDUPE_PASS` after semantic search of Jira SCRUM and GitHub Issues. Adjacent, not duplicate: `SCRUM-395/#388` owns cross-source coherent observation; `SCRUM-183` owns intake context gaps; `SCRUM-568/#513` owns repository-protection capture completeness; `SCRUM-543` only records compare-pagination as a repository-head risk. This research owns provider-neutral **within-source result-set exhaustiveness** for negative/exhaustive decisions.

## REPO EVIDENCE
Reviewed exact current `main`, `AGENTS.md`, and Node Architect governance/research surfaces. Repository search for pagination/cursor/pageInfo/hasNextPage/next_cursor/result-set completeness did not expose a shared Node Architect artifact that binds a connector query to exhaustive collection evidence before negative/dedupe decisions. Existing controls classify incomplete/unavailable evidence carefully, but the reviewed snapshot has no provider-neutral result-set receipt.

## SOURCE EVIDENCE
- GitHub REST documents that large responses are paginated and return only a subset; clients follow `Link` relations such as `rel="next"`: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api
- Slack documents cursor pagination: a non-empty `response_metadata.next_cursor` means more results remain, and receiving fewer than `limit` does not prove completion: https://docs.slack.dev/apis/web-api/pagination/
- Jira Cloud documents paginated collection responses, endpoint-specific limits, actual page sizes that may differ from requested `maxResults`, and optional/changing totals: https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v2/

## INFERENCE
1. A successful connector call proves a response, not exhaustive search-domain coverage.
2. Page length alone cannot generically prove end-of-collection.
3. Negative semantic decisions (`NO_MATCH`, `ABSENT`, `DEDUPE_PASS` where absence matters) require stronger completeness evidence than a positive hit.
4. Pagination completeness and snapshot coherence are orthogonal: all pages can be traversed while a collection changes between pages.
5. Page-complete results can still be domain-incomplete due to permissions or field projection.
6. Collection evidence never grants gate authority.

## PROPOSAL — `ConnectorCollectionReceipt`

```text
schema_version
receipt_id
source_kind
provider_or_connector
operation
query_digest
search_domain
requested_field_profile_digest
permission_scope_digest_or_profile
capture_started_at
capture_completed_at
pages_observed
items_observed
page_chain_digest
continuation_semantics
continuation_exhausted
reported_total_if_available
snapshot_revision_or_etag_if_available
snapshot_stability: STABLE | DRIFTED | UNKNOWN
field_completeness: COMPLETE | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN
domain_completeness: COMPLETE | PERMISSION_SCOPED | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN
collection_status: COMPLETE | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN | FAILED
negative_result_eligible
reason_codes[]
receipt_digest
```

Core invariants:
```text
NEGATIVE_RESULT_REQUIRES_COMPLETE_COLLECTION_PROOF
NONEMPTY_CONTINUATION_MEANS_COLLECTION_NOT_COMPLETE
CLIENT_LIMIT_CANNOT_BE_INTERPRETED_AS_SOURCE_TOTAL
PAGE_CHAIN_OR_SNAPSHOT_DRIFT_INVALIDATES_EXHAUSTIVE_NEGATIVE_DECISION
PARTIAL_FIELD_SEARCH_CANNOT_PROVE_BODY_LEVEL_NONMATCH
PERMISSION_SCOPED_COMPLETENESS_MUST_NOT_BE_RELABELED_GLOBAL_COMPLETENESS
COLLECTION_COMPLETENESS_NEVER_GRANTS_GATE_AUTHORITY
```

Suggested reasons: `COLLECTION_CONTINUATION_REMAINS`, `COLLECTION_PAGE_LIMIT_REACHED`, `COLLECTION_CURSOR_EXPIRED`, `COLLECTION_SNAPSHOT_DRIFT`, `COLLECTION_FIELD_PROJECTION_PARTIAL`, `COLLECTION_PERMISSION_SCOPE_PARTIAL`, `COLLECTION_TOTAL_UNKNOWN`, `COLLECTION_COMPLETENESS_UNKNOWN`, `NEGATIVE_RESULT_NOT_PROVABLE`.

## ASSUMPTIONS
- Supported connector operations expose enough continuation metadata to classify exhaustion; otherwise status is `UNKNOWN`.
- Not every source has a stable snapshot revision; the receipt records `UNKNOWN` instead of inventing one.
- Permission-scoped completeness is valid only when that exact scope is the governed search domain and is recorded explicitly.
- Positive existence checks may stop early; negative/exhaustive decisions may not.

## RISKS
- Exhaustive traversal adds latency, rate-limit pressure and tool/token cost.
- Mutable collections may prevent stable exhaustive scans.
- Ranked/top-N search APIs may not expose exhaustive global-search semantics.
- Permission changes can create mixed visibility across pages.
- Persisting raw result sets can create privacy/cost risk; receipts should remain compact.
- Overuse of exhaustive scans can slow S1/S2, so decision policy must distinguish existence from absence proofs.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Typed `ConnectorCollectionReceipt` binds source/operation/query/search-domain/field-profile and collection evidence.
2. Non-empty continuation prevents `COMPLETE`.
3. Short page length alone never proves completion when provider continuation metadata exists.
4. Negative/exhaustive decisions require `negative_result_eligible=true` from explicit completeness evidence.
5. Top-N caps or unexposed continuation yield `PARTIAL/UNKNOWN`, never silent COMPLETE.
6. Field and permission completeness are represented separately from page exhaustion.
7. Snapshot stability is captured where supported; drift invalidates exhaustive negative evidence.
8. Duplicate items/cursor replay/page-order instability remain deterministic via page-chain/query binding.
9. Rate limits, interruption and cursor expiry defer/resume without false negative.
10. Receipt does not persist unnecessary raw payload and never grants/widens G2-G6 authority.
11. Tests cover GitHub Link pagination, Slack `next_cursor`, Jira page variability, partial fields, permission scope, mutation between pages, cursor expiry and top-N-only search.
12. Observability distinguishes `COMPLETE | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN | FAILED`.

## OUT OF SCOPE
No implementation; no branch/PR/merge/deploy/release/config/data/secret/migration/destructive action. No distributed transaction across sources (`SCRUM-395` remains owner). No requirement to retain whole external result bodies. No claim every semantic search API can prove globally exhaustive absence. No replacement of provider-specific completeness controls.

## SELF-REVIEW
This boundary is narrower than `SCRUM-395/#388`: within-source result-set exhaustiveness vs cross-source coherent observation. It generalizes evidence properties already visible in `SCRUM-183` and `SCRUM-568` without taking over their domains. Permission, field, page and snapshot completeness remain separate dimensions. No formal repository validation PASS is claimed.

## THREE-ROUND FUTURE DELIVERY PLAN
**Round 1 — Inventory + adversarial fixtures:** inventory connector/list/search surfaces used for dedupe/readback/governance evidence; classify continuation/limit/field/permission semantics; fixtures for hidden next page, short page with continuation, top-N cap, partial fields and mutation between pages.

**Round 2 — Shared receipt + decision binding:** schema + provider adapters + deterministic query/page-chain digests; require complete receipt for negative/exhaustive decisions; compose with context-gap and decision-snapshot semantics without granting authority.

**Round 3 — Hardening + rollout/measurement:** rate-limit/cursor-expiry/restart, permission drift and snapshot churn; staged S1/S2 Jira+GitHub dedupe use; measure `collection_partial_rate`, `negative_result_blocked_rate`, `pagination_pages_per_query`, `snapshot_drift_rate`, `cursor_resume_rate`, latency/cost.

items.title: Activate Azure OIDC, integration broker, Microsoft Copilot, and HELIOS platform links
items.body:
## Goal

Complete the live account/tenant side after the paired communication-contract PRs are merged:

- bootstrap PR: `Heli0s-Dynamics/adaptive-multibrain-bootstrap#1`
- platform PR: `M0nado/helios-platform#151`

## GitHub environments and policy

- [ ] Protect `main` in both repositories
- [ ] Require contract/CI checks and pull-request review
- [ ] Create protected environments: `azure-dev`, `azure-test`, `azure-prod`
- [ ] Add approval rules for production
- [ ] Confirm GitHub Copilot coding agent access for the intended repositories
- [ ] Confirm Codex repository access and instruction-file discovery

## Azure identity and broker

- [ ] Create a user-assigned managed identity or Entra application for GitHub OIDC
- [ ] Add federated credentials scoped to each protected GitHub environment
- [ ] Set `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, and `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` as environment variables
- [ ] Grant least privilege at environment resource-group scope
- [ ] Deploy development Key Vault, Service Bus, Event Grid, Storage, Application Insights, and Log Analytics
- [ ] Deploy the integration broker as an Azure Function or Container App
- [ ] Run Bicep validation and `what-if` before deployment
- [ ] Configure private endpoints/DNS where required

## Microsoft Copilot / Copilot Studio / Graph

- [ ] Create the least-privilege Entra app/managed identity for Microsoft Graph operations
- [ ] Define separate permissions for Teams notifications and SharePoint evidence publishing
- [ ] Obtain explicit tenant-admin consent
- [ ] Create an API Management or broker-backed Copilot Studio custom connector
- [ ] Register only approved HELIOS commands; do not expose arbitrary shell or admin execution
- [ ] Create a dedicated Teams development channel for integration tests
- [ ] Create a governed SharePoint development library for runbooks/evidence
- [ ] Define Power Platform/Fabric connections to approved APIs and curated telemetry only
- [ ] Apply Purview classification/retention to published evidence

- [ ] Dispatch a sample GitHub integration event
- [ ] Validate it against the shared event schema
- [ ] Route it through the Azure broker
- [ ] Have `M0nado/helios-platform` acknowledge it without changing workstation state
- [ ] Post a test Teams message
- [ ] Publish a test evidence artifact to SharePoint
- [ ] Preserve the GitHub run, Azure correlation ID, and evidence links
- [ ] Run XCore evaluation and open follow-up issues for missing evidence

## Guardrails

Do not create an Azure client secret when workload identity federation is supported. Do not grant subscription-wide Owner or tenant-wide broad Graph permissions. Microsoft Copilot/Copilot Studio may request operations but cannot bypass GitHub, Azure environment approvals, or privileged-command gates.
